result.summary: Audited the four published lesson pages in range (071, 072, 079, 080; lessons 073-078 have no site/pages/lessons page and were skipped). All four fail the audit criteria in the same systemic way. (1) Flow: each page is a specification dump — safety banners, reason-code and precedence tables, struct/API listings, byte layouts, and resource/fingerprint tables — with no build narrative; findings rate all four high. (2) Hands-on: the only activity in each lesson is a single abstract predict/observe table for a compile-only Mega replay, with no concrete inputs, calls, or expected values a learner can execute step by step. (3) Assessment: every PDF (docs/lessons/NNN/main.tex) ends with a standalone Exercises section (071 line 331, 072 line 284, 079 line 318, 080 line 327, the last also with a fill-in acceptance-record box); all flagged for folding into the lesson steps. (4) Drawings: asset counts are 071: 5, 072: 3, 079: 4, 080: 4 pencil pairs, and every one is a concept diagram (arithmetic flow boxes, envelopes, ledgers, gates); there are zero assembly visuals — no breadboard, wiring, module pinout, transistor schematic sketch, or even a board-and-USB setup drawing — and the HTML pages embed no images at all, so web learners see no visuals whatsoever. 14-finding cap respected by consolidating the cross-lesson drawing gap into the 079 and 080 asset findings.

findings.issue: Every sketch hand-writes the same initialize-all/rollback ceremony: call initialize() on each component, AND the .ok() results, and on failure shutdown everything in reverse order (initializeHardware/shutdownHardware in Lesson006, initializeCircuit/stopSafely in Lesson009, acquireCircuit in Lesson010). The library itself repeats the identical rollback chain inside RgbLed::initialize (3 PwmOutputs) and ShiftRegisterOutput::initialize (3 DigitalOutputs). There is no seam that owns 'bring up N components, unwind on first failure'.
findings.recommendation: Add a small ComponentGroup/InitScope helper (array of pointers to a minimal Initializable seam with initialize/shutdown) that initializes in order and unwinds in reverse on failure. Use it inside RgbLed and ShiftRegisterOutput and in the lesson sketches; this deletes the largest single block of boilerplate in every consumer.
findings.where: examples/Lesson006Simon/Lesson006Simon.ino:191-227 (pattern repeated across ~24 sketches; internally in src/rgb_led.cpp:113-135 and src/shift_register.cpp:46-70)

findings.issue: The monotonic-time guard — lastUpdate_ + hasLastUpdate_ + timeValid(now) + a private maximumDuration = 0x7fffffff constant — is copy-pasted into every time-driven policy object, starting with ReactionTimer and Simon in this group. Each type re-derives the same wraparound-safe validity rule and carries three extra members for it.
findings.recommendation: Extract a small UpdateClock (or MonotonicGuard) type into time.h owning lastUpdate/hasLastUpdate/validity and the half-range constant; policies compose it. This removes three fields and one private method from every policy and makes the timing rule single-sourced.
findings.where: src/reaction_timer.cpp:202 and src/simon.cpp:413 (same triple in 10+ policy types: access_trainer, bounded_homing_policy, bounded_stepper_sequence, calibration_console, keypad, motor_intent, percussion_sequencer, rover_controller, ...)

findings.issue: Button has no way to export its own state: ButtonObservation (pressed/pressEvent/releaseEvent) is defined in the consumer header reaction_timer.h, reaction_timer.cpp writes a private observe() adapter to fill it, balance_table_instrument reinvents the same three fields as BalanceButtonObservation, and the Simon sketch hand-assembles activeMask/pressedMask/releasedMask from four Buttons field by field. The observation type of the physical component lives everywhere except with the component, and ReactionTimer's update(TimePoint, const Button&) overload couples a pure policy to the hardware driver to compensate.
findings.recommendation: Move ButtonObservation into button.h and give Button an observation() (snapshot-style) accessor; have ReactionTimer, BalanceTableInstrument, and the Simon mask-assembly loop consume it. Consider a small ButtonBank helper that owns the update-N-buttons-and-build-masks loop Simon-style callers repeat.

findings.issue: MicrosecondDuration/MicrosecondTimePoint are structural clones of Duration/TimePoint (same Raw alias, ctor, accessor, elapsedSince) but live inside pulse_input.h — a specific driver-policy header — and lack the comparison operators the millisecond types have. Sibling arcs (ultrasonic_ranger.h, pulse_capture/mega_pulse_capture_io) include pulse_input.h just to obtain the microsecond time vocabulary.
findings.recommendation: Move the microsecond types into time.h beside Duration/TimePoint (or a shared unit-tagged template) with the same operator set, and let pulse_input.h include time.h. This fixes both the misplaced seam and the operator drift between the unit families.

findings.issue: TimePoint/Duration are too thin for real call sites: no TimePoint + Duration, no Duration arithmetic, no deadline helper. Consequently the sketches abandon the vocabulary and fall back to raw uint32_t millis() math with hand-written wraparound casts (runStarted/inactiveStarted as uint32_t in Lesson006, nextTelemetryAt = now + interval in Lesson009), so the type exists but callers route around it precisely where wraparound bugs live.
findings.recommendation: Add TimePoint operator+(Duration), Duration addition/comparison already exists — plus a Deadline/elapsed>=duration helper (e.g. bool TimePoint::reached(TimePoint start, Duration d)). Then convert the lesson sketches to stay in the vocabulary end to end.

findings.issue: The file is named sampled_signal but contains no SampledSignal: only three independent stages (LinearCalibration, MovingAverage, Deadband). Both consuming lessons hand-chain calibrate -> average -> deadband with per-stage Result unwrap-and-bail ceremony, and Lesson009 additionally hand-classifies below/above-range faults before the chain — exactly the pipeline the filename promises as one object.
findings.recommendation: Add a SampledSignal composite that owns the three stages (and optional valid-range classification), exposing addSample(raw) -> Result/snapshot with a fault state. Lessons 8 and 9 shrink to one call per loop and the fault taxonomy stops being sketch-local.

findings.issue: ThresholdInput deviates from every sibling policy convention in the library: no initialize()/initialized() (constructor + reset() instead), state accessor named observation() where 61 other headers use snapshot(), and update() returns the observation struct instead of Status with faults carried in a member enum rather than the Status field siblings embed in their snapshots. Consistent with the drift, no sketch has ever adopted it (only its unit test and Adk.h reference it) even though docs/design/sensor_component_families.md directs sensor families to use it.
findings.recommendation: Align it with the established policy shape — initialize()/initialized(), snapshot() naming, Status-bearing snapshot — before more sensor arcs are built against the documented recommendation.

findings.issue: Two different pin-validity authorities coexist for the same board: digital primitives validate with the raw NUM_DIGITAL_PINS macro while analog/PWM primitives consult the Mega2560Board capability table. RgbLed additionally re-runs validPin/supports per channel even though the PwmOutput::initialize it then calls performs the identical checks, so the same pin is validated twice through two seams.
findings.recommendation: Route all pin validation through the board capability seam (Mega2560Board::validPin/supports, adding a DigitalIo capability if needed) and drop RgbLed's duplicate channel validation, keeping only its resistorOhms and distinct-pin checks.
findings.where: src/digital_input.cpp:31, src/digital_output.cpp:31, src/piezo_sounder.cpp:32, src/shift_register.cpp:32-34 vs src/analog_input.cpp:33-38, src/pwm_output.cpp:34-42, src/rgb_led.cpp:8-28

findings.issue: NightLight re-implements the activate-below/deactivate-above hysteresis state machine inline (turnOnBelowPermille/turnOffAbovePermille plus mode flipping) that ThresholdInput exists to own (activateAt/deactivateAt with direction and fault classification). Two implementations of the same physical concept — a hysteretic threshold on a bounded reading — now live in the group and can drift independently.
findings.recommendation: Compose a Falling-direction ThresholdInput inside NightLight (or once ThresholdInput's conventions are fixed per the other finding), leaving NightLight to own only duty selection and fault presentation.

findings.issue: Re-running initialize() on an already-initialized MonoLed desynchronizes cached state from hardware: DigitalOutput::initialize early-returns Ok without rewriting the pin, but MonoLed unconditionally resets active_ = false. After on(); initialize(); the object reports active() == false while the LED is physically lit, and the same early-return pattern means RgbLed keeps its old color_ but SevenSegmentDisplay keeps its old glyph while claiming a fresh lifecycle.
findings.recommendation: On the already-initialized path, either drive the output to the inactive level (set(false)) before clearing active_, or leave cached state untouched to match the hardware; pick one re-initialize contract and apply it across the wrapper components.

findings.issue: ButtonConfig is the only config in the group with a user-declared constructor, while RgbLedChannel, ShiftRegisterPins, ThresholdInputConfig, NightLightConfig, SimonConfig are aggregates with member defaults. The ctor prevents brace/designated initialization and, combined with Button taking config by reference, pushes sketches into declaring a named const config per button — Lesson006 spends eight namespace-scope declarations to build four buttons.
findings.recommendation: Make ButtonConfig an aggregate with default member initializers (matching sibling configs) and/or add a Button(ResourceRegistry&, PinId) convenience for the default pull-up/active-low case, collapsing the per-button config declarations.

findings.issue: The read()/sample() naming is inverted relative to the physical mental model: sample() is the method that touches hardware (despite being const) and read() returns the cached value from the last update(). Callers wanting the loop-consistent value must know to pair update() then read(), and the const hardware-touching sample() is an easy wrong choice.
findings.recommendation: Rename toward intent — e.g. level()/reading() for the cached value and keep update() as the sole hardware touchpoint (or name the live read sampleHardware()) — so the cached accessor no longer sounds like an I/O operation and vice versa.

findings.issue: Sibling stages in the same header disagree on their result contract: MovingAverage::addSample and LinearCalibration::map return Result<uint16_t>, while Deadband::addSample returns a bare uint16_t (though Deadband::value() returns Result). Pipeline call sites in Lessons 8-9 must switch error-handling style mid-chain.
findings.recommendation: Return Result<uint16_t> from Deadband::addSample for a uniform stage interface (which also makes the missing SampledSignal composite trivial to write over a common stage shape).

result.summary: Audited the core-primitives group (status/time/digital IO, LEDs, button, sounder, analog/threshold/pulse inputs, shift register, seven-segment, night light, sampled signal, reaction timer, simon) plus consuming lessons 1-10 and their tests. The relationship model is mostly clean composition (Button->DigitalInput, MonoLed->DigitalOutput, RgbLed->3xPwmOutput, SevenSegmentDisplay->ShiftRegisterOutput->3xDigitalOutput; CueSource is the group's one virtual seam and is well used). The three severe problems are missing seams that force repetition: (1) no init-group/rollback helper, so every sketch and every composite hand-writes initialize-all + reverse-shutdown chains; (2) the monotonic-time guard (lastUpdate_/hasLastUpdate_/timeValid/0x7fffffff) is copy-pasted across 10+ policy types starting with ReactionTimer and Simon; (3) Button cannot export its own observation — ButtonObservation lives in reaction_timer.h, balance_table_instrument clones it, and the Simon sketch hand-builds masks. Secondary issues: microsecond time types are structural clones of Duration/TimePoint stranded in pulse_input.h; TimePoint/Duration are too thin so sketches revert to raw millis() math; sampled_signal.h names a composite that does not exist while two lessons hand-chain its stages; ThresholdInput drifts from every policy convention (observation() vs snapshot(), no initialize) and NightLight duplicates its hysteresis; pin validation splits between NUM_DIGITAL_PINS and the Mega2560Board capability seam; re-initialize can desync MonoLed cached state from hardware. Read-only audit; no files modified.

findings.issue: StableRecord's invariant (length <= capacity of 96) is owned by nobody. StorageRecordSink::append passes record.length straight to storage_->append without validating it, so a StableRecord with length in 97..255 causes a read past the end of record.text (up to 159 bytes OOB) whenever the medium has room. Every producer (tests' recordWith helper, telemetry_record.cpp) must independently remember to clamp; the type itself is a bare struct that cannot defend itself.
findings.recommendation: Either give StableRecord a setter/factory that clamps or rejects oversized text, or have StorageRecordSink::append return InvalidArgument when record.length > StableRecord::capacity. One line in append closes the OOB hole.

findings.issue: When endTransaction fails, MegaSpiDriver::transfer self-destructs (io_->disable, configured_=false, releaseClaims) but has no channel to tell its owner. SpiBus::initialized_ stays true and SpiDevice::initialized_ stays true, so after this failure bus.initialized() and device.initialized() both report true while every transfer returns NotInitialized. Callers cannot distinguish 'never initialized' from 'driver died mid-transfer' and have no signal that a full bus shutdown/initialize cycle is the required recovery.
findings.recommendation: Propagate the fatal state upward: have SpiBus::transfer treat a NotInitialized/restore-failure result from a configured driver as bus death (clear initialized_, release the bus claim), or return a distinct StatusCode (e.g. HardwareFailure) so the layers stay consistent.

findings.issue: SpiDevice::initialize reaches through the friend seam into bus_->resources_ to claim its chip-select pin, and also performs the Unsupported->InvalidPin status mapping itself. The I2C sibling keeps all shared bookkeeping behind I2cBus::attach/detach; the SPI arc splits ownership of 'device admission' between bus (configureDevice) and device (pin claim), so the two structurally-parallel arcs have different responsibility boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Move the chip-select pin claim (and the status mapping) into SpiBus::configureDevice/releaseDevice so the bus owns device admission exactly as I2cBus does, and SpiDevice no longer needs to touch bus privates beyond the narrow attach/transfer calls.

findings.issue: acquireBusOwners is nine consecutive 'status = x.initialize(); if (!ok) { observeFailure; return false; }' blocks (~75 lines), and stopSafely (lines 425-444) hand-maintains the reverse-order shutdown ladder. The bus stack knows its own dependency order (bus before device) yet offers no composite: every sketch that owns a bus plus devices (Lesson022, Lesson024, Lesson060, Lesson063 show the same ladder shape) re-encodes ordering and unwind by hand, and a misordered call is only caught at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Give the bus arc a small aggregate seam, e.g. I2cBus/SpiBus initialize their attached devices, or an adk::InitializerList/Session helper that initializes an ordered set of components, stops at the first failure, and shuts down in reverse. Sketches shrink to one call plus one failure handler.

findings.issue: The Mega pin-to-external-interrupt map is encoded three times: PulseCapture::interruptFor, mega_pulse_capture_io.cpp:21-31 interruptFor, and board.cpp:17-22 externalInterruptPin. Worse, PulseCapture is the hardware-agnostic policy layer (it talks through PulseCaptureIo) yet hard-codes Mega2560 pin numbers, defeating the Io seam. Mega2560Board already sets the precedent for this exact kind of query with pwmTimer(pin, timer&).
findings.recommendation: Add Mega2560Board::externalInterrupt(pin, index&) (mirroring pwmTimer) and have both the board capability check and MegaPulseCaptureIo use it; let PulseCapture obtain the interrupt index through PulseCaptureIo (or its config) instead of owning a Mega pin table.

findings.issue: ResourceClaim and SharedResourceClaim are line-for-line identical types (same fields, same deleted operations, same active/release shape, duplicated ctor/dtor/release bodies in resource.cpp:14-62); the only behavioral difference is which registry release method the destructor routes to. Any future change (e.g. making claims movable) must be made twice.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to one claim type that records whether it is shared (or have the registry dispatch on ResourceKind bookkeeping), or factor a common base holding registry_/resource_/active/release with the release hook as the single point of variation.

findings.issue: I2cBus and SpiBus constructor/initialize/shutdown/initialized are structural duplicates (i2c_bus.cpp:17-80 vs spi_bus.cpp:15-72): claim {kind, 0}, driver configure, disable+release on failure, mirrored shutdown. The anonymous-namespace validTimeout helper is also copied verbatim into both files. A third owned bus (serial is already a ResourceKind) would mean a third copy.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared 'owned bus' lifecycle (registry claim + configure/disable pairing + initialized flag) into a small base or helper parameterized by ResourceKind and driver, and move validTimeout to a shared header (or onto Duration).

findings.issue: Storage has append/sync but no way to drop staged bytes, so StorageRecordSink::discardStaged fakes a rollback by calling storage shutdown+initialize, temporarily flipping its own initialized_ flag. If the re-initialize fails, append returns the rollback status (masking the original append/sync error) and the sink is silently left uninitialized even though the caller never asked for shutdown.
findings.recommendation: Add Status discard() (or rollback()) to the Storage interface -- FixedStorage implements it as stagedSize_ = medium_->durableSize_ -- and let append report the original failure while the sink stays initialized.

findings.issue: injectAppendFailureAt/injectSyncFailure are public API on FixedStorage, the same object Lesson022 uses as its real storage component. Fault injection knobs on the shipped type fight the mental model of a storage component, and the codebase already has a convention for this: PulseCapture exposes test internals through a 'friend struct PulseCaptureTestAccess' seam instead (pulse_capture.h:52,95).
findings.recommendation: Move the failure injection behind a FixedStorageTestAccess friend (matching the PulseCaptureTestAccess convention) or into a failure-injecting Storage decorator used only by tests.

findings.issue: Rtc is an interface with no concrete implementation anywhere in src/ (rtc.cpp is only the destructor), so every consumer hand-rolls a near-identical simulated clock: SimulatedRtc in Lesson022 (line 28), SimulatedRtc in Lesson024 (line 31), FixtureRtc in Lesson036 (line 26), FakeRtc in test_magnetic_passage_logger.cpp (line 11). For an inert USB-only curriculum this is the storage arc's exact situation, and there the library ships FixedStorage; the clock arc lacks the equivalent.
findings.recommendation: Ship an adk::SimulatedRtc (monotonic seconds from a seed, settable ClockState) alongside the interface, mirroring how FixedStorage serves as the in-library Storage, and delete the four per-sketch copies.

findings.issue: Runtime is a pass-through holding one ResourceRegistry with a single accessor, yet all 42 sketches declare 'adk::Runtime runtime;' and then repeat 'runtime.resources()' at every component constructor (Lesson022 alone calls it five times). The name promises a board runtime; the type delivers nothing beyond the registry, so the extra layer is pure call-site ceremony.
findings.recommendation: Either grow Runtime into the real composition root (registry + board identity + time source, with components accepting Runtime&) or drop it and have sketches declare the ResourceRegistry directly.

findings.issue: Within this one group the three abstract lifecycles disagree on whether initialized() is part of the contract: RecordSink declares 'virtual bool initialized() const' (record_sink.h:26), while Storage and Rtc omit it -- FixedStorage adds a non-virtual initialized() that is invisible through the Storage interface. Code holding a Storage& or Rtc& cannot query lifecycle state the way it can for every concrete component and for RecordSink.
findings.recommendation: Add initialized() to Storage and Rtc (FixedStorage already implements it), aligning the group's interfaces with the initialize/shutdown/initialized triple used by every concrete component in the library.

findings.issue: ResourceRegistry hard-codes Mega2560 topology (70 pins, 6 timers, 6 interrupts, 4 serial ports, and the bit-offset layout at lines 187-213) under a board-neutral name, while Mega2560Board exists precisely to own board facts and is never consulted. The generically named type silently becomes wrong on any other board, and the counts live in a different file than the board's own capability tables.
findings.recommendation: Source the per-kind counts from Mega2560Board constants (or rename the type Mega2560ResourceRegistry) so board topology has a single owner and the registry's board coupling is explicit.

findings.issue: FixedStorageMedium's constructor accepts any capacity (0 or above maximumCapacity) without complaint; the invalid descriptor is only diagnosed later and at a different object, when FixedStorage::initialize returns InvalidArgument (lines 44-47). The error surfaces at a distance from the mistake, and a medium constructed with capacity 600 still reports capacity() == 600 while backed by a 512-byte array.
findings.recommendation: Clamp or normalize capacity in the FixedStorageMedium constructor (e.g. store min(capacity, maximumCapacity) and expose a valid() query), so the descriptor object cannot exist in a state its own accessors misreport.

result.summary: Audited the runtime-resources-buses group (board, runtime, resource, power_domain, i2c/spi buses, mega drivers/io, pulse-capture io, storage, rtc, record_sink, observation_tracker) plus Lesson022 and the group's tests. The group's initialize/shutdown/initialized lifecycle discipline is generally consistent with sibling arcs, and PowerDomain, ObservationTracker, and the driver/io layering are clean. The 14 findings: two severe -- StableRecord's length invariant is unenforced at StorageRecordSink::append (latent OOB read), and MegaSpiDriver's failure path silently kills the driver while SpiBus/SpiDevice keep reporting initialized; several structural issues -- SpiDevice bypasses the bus seam to claim its CS pin (unlike the I2C sibling), the Mega interrupt map is triplicated with the hardware-agnostic PulseCapture hard-coding Mega pins, ResourceClaim/SharedResourceClaim and I2cBus/SpiBus are copy-paste twins, Storage lacks a discard primitive forcing a shutdown/initialize rollback hack, and FixedStorage carries public fault-injection hooks contrary to the TestAccess convention; plus call-site ceremony -- every sketch hand-rolls the same 9-block initialize ladder and reverse shutdown ladder, four consumers each reimplement a simulated Rtc the library never ships, and Runtime is a vestigial one-accessor wrapper repeated across 42 sketches. Minor drift: initialized() missing from the Storage/Rtc interfaces but present on RecordSink, Mega2560 topology hard-coded in the board-neutral ResourceRegistry, and FixedStorageMedium deferring capacity validation to a different object.

findings.issue: BoundedServo (position policy) and ServoOutput (pulse hardware) have no connecting type, so every caller hand-wires the pipeline: admit gate -> servo.command(position) -> servo.snapshot() -> pulseOutput.writePulse(snapshot.pulseUs) -> revoke gate on each failure branch. Lesson017's startSafeWaveform() and commandPosition() are 20-line near-duplicates of exactly this sequence. The caller must also feed the same pulse limits twice: BoundedServoConfig.calibration.minimumPulseUs/maximumPulseUs into BoundedServo AND the identical values into the ServoOutput constructor (Lesson017:27-31); if they drift, commands the policy considers legal are rejected by the output at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Add a composing type (e.g. BoundedServoDrive) owning a BoundedServo, a ServoOutput, and the PowerDomain interplay, exposing command(position)/safe()/snapshot(); derive ServoOutput's limits from the single ServoCalibrationConfig so the bounds have one source of truth.

findings.issue: Every sketch hand-writes the same two ceremonies: an initialize staircase where each failing initialize() must roll back all prior components in reverse (Lesson018's acquireTrainerCircuit is ~50 lines of pyramid-shaped shutdown calls), and a stopSafely()/shutdownJunction() that re-lists every component in reverse acquisition order. All group types share the exact initialize()/shutdown() duck-typed protocol, but there is no shared Component interface and no aggregate helper (Runtime owns only the ResourceRegistry), so this ordering logic cannot be factored out and is re-derived, error-prone, in every lesson.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a minimal lifecycle interface (Status initialize(), void shutdown()) implemented by the peripheral types, plus a small fixed-capacity aggregate (e.g. ComponentChain) that initializes in order with rollback on failure and shuts down in reverse; sketches then declare the order once.

findings.issue: UltrasonicRanger models only the echo half of an HC-SR04: the trigger side (own a DigitalOutput, drive it high, blocking delayMicroseconds(10), drive low, then call startMeasurement with a freshly sampled echo level) is caller-owned boilerplate (Lesson019 requestRange), as is the measurementComplete() four-state check needed before re-triggering. The type also drifts from every sibling's conventions: it exposes reading()/reset() instead of snapshot()/shutdown(), and RangeReading carries no Status while KeypadSnapshot, TrafficSnapshot, MotorIntentSnapshot, AccessSnapshot, and RoverControllerSnapshot all do; RangeReading.valid duplicates state == RangeState::Valid.
findings.recommendation: Either fold trigger sequencing into the ranger (constructor takes the trigger pin/output, expose requestMeasurement(now)) or add an HcSr04 composing type; rename reading()->snapshot(), add shutdown(), give the reading a Status, and drop the redundant valid flag.

findings.issue: AccessLedIntent is a member-for-member copy of AccessState (Ready/Entering/Granted/Denied/LockedOut/Fault) and AccessTrainer::ledIntent() is a pure identity-mapping switch. AccessSnapshot then carries four overlapping representations of two facts: state AND ledIntent, plus softLatchIntent (enum) AND softLatchOpen (bool) which are always derived from state == Granted. Consumers (Lesson018 stateColor) just switch on the mirror enum.
findings.recommendation: Delete AccessLedIntent and have presentation code switch on AccessState directly (the abstraction adds no indirection value while the enums are 1:1); keep either softLatchIntent or softLatchOpen, not both.

findings.issue: RangeReading carries no observation timestamp, yet RoverInput requires rangeObservedAt as a millisecond TimePoint while the ranger operates entirely in MicrosecondTimePoint. The caller must remember the completion instant itself and hand-convert domains: adk::TimePoint (rangeObservedAtUs.microseconds () / 1000U) (Lesson021:243). The ranger already knows the time the echo completed (it is passed to update()) but discards it, forcing every rover integrator to reconstruct it and own a lossy unit conversion at the seam between the two types.
findings.recommendation: Stamp the completion MicrosecondTimePoint into RangeReading when the state becomes Valid/OutOfRange/Timeout, and give the library one sanctioned microsecond->millisecond conversion (or accept the microsecond timestamp in RoverInput and convert inside RoverController against config).

findings.issue: formatClimateRecord — a serial telemetry-record formatter over ClimateSample — lives in character_display.h/cpp, which therefore #includes climate_sensor.h. The function never touches CharacterDisplay; it is consumed by Lessons 014/015 to print to Serial. Every display consumer (keypad trainers, greenhouse, timing desk) transitively pulls climate-sensor types, and the display translation unit carries RecordWriter formatting machinery unrelated to the HD44780.
findings.recommendation: Move formatClimateRecord (and RecordWriter) next to the climate types (climate_sensor.* or a climate_record.* unit) and drop the climate_sensor.h include from character_display.h.

findings.issue: The servo family is split across three near-synonymous headers whose names do not say where things live: the actual servo policy (BoundedServo, BoundedServoConfig, BoundedServoIntent, BoundedServoSnapshot) hides in servo_calibration.h; servo_configuration.h is not configuration of a servo but a persistence codec (ServoConfigurationRecord); servo_output.h holds the waveform driver. A reader looking for 'the servo type' has no file named for it, and 'calibration' vs 'configuration' invite the wrong include.
findings.recommendation: Move BoundedServo* into a bounded_servo.h (matching Lesson017BoundedServo naming) leaving servo_calibration.h with only ServoCalibration; rename servo_configuration.* to servo_configuration_record.* or fold it beside the storage types.

findings.issue: The absolute servo pulse envelope (544/2400 us) is defined twice with no reference between them: ServoOutput::absoluteMinimumPulseUs/absoluteMaximumPulseUs (public constexpr) and independent anonymous-namespace constants minimumSupportedPulseUs/maximumSupportedPulseUs in servo_calibration.cpp. servo_calibration.cpp does not include servo_output.h, so nothing forces them to agree; if one envelope is ever adjusted, ServoCalibration would validate pulses that ServoOutput rejects (or vice versa) with no compile-time signal.
findings.recommendation: Define the envelope once (e.g. constants in a small servo_limits.h or on ServoCalibration, which ServoOutput references) so both validators share one source.

findings.issue: The hardware-seam injection style differs per type within the group: MatrixKeypad takes an optional trailing raw pointer (MatrixKeypadIo* io = nullptr, nullptr meaning a hidden global Arduino IO), Hd44780Display and MegaTimer5ServoPulseIo use a reference overload pair (default ctor binds a file-static transport), while PulseCapture and ServoOutput require the IO reference outright. Test authors and lesson readers must learn three idioms for the same 'swap the electronics for a fake' seam.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on the overloaded-constructor-with-reference pattern (already the majority) and drop the nullable-pointer parameter from MatrixKeypad.

findings.issue: MegaTimer5ServoPulseIo hard-fixes its identity (signalPin = 44, timer = 5) yet ServoOutput's constructor makes the caller restate both back to it (adk::MegaTimer5ServoPulseIo::signalPin, adk::MegaTimer5ServoPulseIo::timer) purely so attach() can verify they match; any mismatch is only discovered at initialize() as Unsupported. The caller is transcribing facts the IO object already owns.
findings.recommendation: Let ServoPulseIo expose pin()/timer() (or attach() return them) so ServoOutput derives identity from its IO, keeping explicit overrides only for genuinely configurable IOs.

findings.issue: Mid-life restart verbs are inconsistent across the group: TrafficJunction::reset() -> Status (no time argument), AccessTrainer::reset(TimePoint now) -> Status, UltrasonicRanger::reset() -> void, MotorIntent uses stop() -> Status, and RoverController has no method at all (restart is signaled through RoverInput.startEvent). Callers moving between components in one sketch cannot predict the restart signature, and the newer arcs (SmallIndicatorSemanticsPolicy) have settled on Status reset() noexcept, which only one of these matches.
findings.recommendation: Converge on the newer arc's Status reset() shape (taking TimePoint where re-anchoring is needed) across the group.

findings.issue: KeypadSnapshot exposes fault through two channels that every consumer must OR together: state == KeypadState::Fault and !status.ok(). Lesson016 writes '!observation.status.ok () || observation.state == adk::KeypadState::Fault' and AccessTrainer::update repeats the same compound test (plus input.componentFault). Since Keypad::snapshot() sets state=Fault exactly when status is HardwareFailure, the double-check is defensive noise each caller re-invents.
findings.recommendation: Document/guarantee that state == Fault iff snapshot status is not ok (or add a single bool healthy()/faulted accessor on the snapshot) so consumers test one thing.

findings.issue: MatrixKeypad is named generically but hard-codes a 4-row x 3-column geometry via individually named pin fields (row0..row3, column0..column2), and Keypad::keyFromMask hard-codes the 12-key telephone layout; the physical component in the lessons is a 4x4 membrane pad operated in 12-key mode with its fourth column insulated (Lesson016/018 comments). Supporting the pad's real A-D column would require a parallel sibling type rather than a wider config, and the generic name oversells what the type represents.
findings.recommendation: Either parameterize row/column counts and the key map (bounded arrays in MatrixKeypadPins/KeypadConfig) or name the pair for what it is (e.g. TwelveKeyMatrixKeypad) so the 4x3 constraint is part of the mental model.

findings.issue: Optional-display handling is smeared through the sketch: six call sites guard with 'useDisplay ? display.update (now) : adk::Status ()' or if (useDisplay) around show()/shutdown(), even though the CharacterDisplay interface exists precisely to abstract the presentation target. The Hd44780Display object is also constructed (pins named, registry bound) even when the build flag disables it.
findings.recommendation: Provide a NullCharacterDisplay implementation of CharacterDisplay (initialize/update/show all Ok, ready() true) so sketches select the implementation once and drop the per-call branching.

result.summary: Audit of the io-appliances group (character_display, matrix_keypad/keypad, servo_output/calibration/configuration, motor_intent, rover_controller, ultrasonic_ranger, pulse_capture, traffic_junction, access_trainer) in /home/ksh/git/adk. The group's core observe/decide/actuate split with config->initialize->update->snapshot lifecycles is internally consistent and well-seamed for testing (Hd44780Transport, MatrixKeypadIo, ServoPulseIo, PulseCaptureIo all have fakes; CharacterDisplay's abstract base is genuinely consumed by greenhouse_controller). The two severe problems are ergonomic: (1) the servo stack has no type composing BoundedServo with ServoOutput and the PowerDomain gate, so callers duplicate a 20-line command pipeline and must keep pulse bounds consistent across two constructors (with the 544/2400 envelope additionally defined twice in the sources); (2) every sketch hand-writes an initialize-with-rollback staircase and a reverse-order shutdown list because the uniform initialize/shutdown protocol has no shared interface or aggregate helper. UltrasonicRanger is the group's convention outlier (reading()/reset() instead of snapshot()/shutdown(), no Status in its reading, no trigger-side modeling, and a caller-owned microsecond-to-millisecond conversion at the RoverController seam). Smaller items: AccessLedIntent mirrors AccessState 1:1 with redundant snapshot fields, formatClimateRecord couples the display header to climate_sensor, the BoundedServo policy hides in servo_calibration.h beside a persistence-codec header named servo_configuration.h, and injection style, restart verbs, and keypad fault signaling drift between siblings. Fourteen findings reported, most severe first; no files were modified.

findings.issue: EnvironmentalStation::chooseHealth maps sensorStatus == StatusCode::InvalidArgument to EnvironmentalHealth::TimingFault, but Dht11Sensor::update also returns InvalidArgument when a checksum-valid frame fails range validation (TemperatureOutOfRange/HumidityOutOfRange). A plain bad reading is therefore classified as a timing fault, and Lesson015 (loop, lines 105-111) halts the whole station on TimingFault + !status.ok — so one out-of-range DHT11 frame permanently halts the sketch as if the clock were broken. InvalidArgument means three different physical things in this group (clock ambiguity, bad config, bad reading).
findings.recommendation: Classify from the sample state, which already carries the distinction: check sample.state == TemperatureOutOfRange/HumidityOutOfRange -> SensorFault before the sensorStatus branch, and reserve the TimingFault branch for sample.state == InvalidTiming (or introduce a dedicated timing status code returned by update on ambiguous elapsed time).

findings.issue: The climate arc defines an abstract ClimateSensor with a RecordedClimateSensor test double, and the pump side defines abstract PumpOutput, but MoistureSensor is concrete-only. GreenhouseController and WateringController take MoistureSensor&/MoistureSample from the concrete type, so every consumer test must assemble ResourceRegistry + AnalogInput + calibration and drive readings through fake::setAnalogInput (test_greenhouse_controller.cpp Fixture at 189-219, requireInvalidConfig at 221-249 rebuilds the 7-object graph, ~15 fake::setAnalogInput calls). The one sensor in the group without a seam is the one the biggest controller composes.
findings.recommendation: Extract a MoistureSource interface (initialize/shutdown/initialized/update/sample) mirroring ClimateSensor, make the analog implementation one subtype, and add a Recorded/Fake sibling like RecordedClimateSensor so controller tests and future sketches stop plumbing the analog stack.

findings.issue: Dht11Sensor has a Dht11Transport seam, but initialize(), shutdown(), and the tail of transact() call pinMode(dataPin_, INPUT) directly instead of releaseLine()/transport, so even with a scripted transport the sensor mutates global Arduino pin state and host tests must link the Arduino fake and assert via adk::test::arduino::mode() (test_dht11_sensor.cpp:127,186,214). Separately, the transport is optional (two constructors, transport_ null checks in five wrapper methods driveLow/releaseLine/readLine/waitUs/nowUs), interleaving the hardware path with the test path.
findings.recommendation: Route all line manipulation through the transport (transact's final restore should be releaseLine()), and replace the nullable-transport branches with a default-constructed ArduinoDht11Transport instance selected in the two-argument constructor, leaving one unconditional code path.

findings.issue: The freshness/InvalidTiming policy in sample() is duplicated verbatim between RecordedClimateSensor and Dht11Sensor (same maximumUnambiguousDuration constant re-declared in both .cpps), and the ClimateSensor interface forces every implementation to re-derive it — test_environmental_station.cpp's FakeClimateSensor (lines 69-81) already drifted to a third variant that silently omits InvalidTiming. Staleness is a property of the sample plus the clock, not of any particular sensor.
findings.recommendation: Hoist the policy next to validateClimateSample as a free function, e.g. ClimateSample applyFreshness(ClimateSample, TimePoint now, Duration staleAfter) noexcept, and have implementations (and fakes) return applyFreshness(sample_, now, staleAfter); alternatively make sample() non-virtual in a small base that owns sample_.

findings.issue: GreenhouseController exposes five per-tick phases (observe/decide/actuate/present/record) with strict-ordering guards that return InvalidArgument on misuse, yet the controller already owns all phase scheduling internally (sample/display/record intervals), so every caller just invokes all five in fixed order every tick: Lesson024 defines five one-line wrapper functions and chains them, and test_greenhouse_controller.cpp repeats the observe/decide/actuate triple ~20 times. Sibling arcs (traffic_junction.h:77, access_trainer.h:100) use a single update(now, input). actuate(TimePoint) also ignores its parameter.
findings.recommendation: Add a composed Status update(TimePoint now, const GreenhouseInput& input) noexcept that runs the pipeline in order (keeping the phase methods, if at all, as private steps or for the lesson narrative), and drop or use actuate's dead TimePoint parameter.

findings.issue: The reverse-unwind initialize ladder (init child A; on failure shutdown A and every prior child; repeat) is hand-written in GreenhouseController::initialize (four children, four progressively longer rollback blocks), EnvironmentalStation::initialize, WateringController::initialize, GreenhouseHealthPattern::initialize, and again by user code in every sketch (acquireStation, acquireGreenhouse, EvidenceRecordSink::initialize). Each copy must get the rollback order exactly right, and the tests spend testInitializationFailureAtEveryDependency (838-line file) proving each hand-written ladder.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a tiny lifecycle seam — e.g. an abstract Component {initialize/shutdown/initialized} that the leaf types already structurally satisfy, plus a helper that initializes an ordered span of Component* with automatic reverse rollback — and build composites and sketches on it.

findings.issue: greenhouse_health_pattern.h includes greenhouse_controller.h solely for the GreenhouseMode enum, pulling the entire controller (and transitively character_display, record_sink, watering_controller, moisture_sensor) into any translation unit that only wants the LED pattern. Because the pattern sits outside the controller's composition, Lesson024 must run a second interleaved init/rollback ladder for it, feed it snapshot().mode by hand each tick, and mirror the shutdown ordering in stopSafely().
findings.recommendation: Move GreenhouseMode (and GreenhouseInput/GreenhouseSnapshot if useful) into a small greenhouse_types.h both headers include; consider letting GreenhouseController optionally own the health pattern as a fifth child so callers get one lifecycle and no manual mode piping.

findings.issue: MoistureSensor::sample checks only elapsedSince(observedAt) > staleAfter with no ambiguity guard and no InvalidTiming-style state (MoistureSampleState has no such member), while its climate siblings treat ages beyond INT32_MAX ms as InvalidTiming. After ~24.8 days without update() the wrapped age makes an ancient sample read as fresh/Valid — and WateringController::decide would happily water on it. update(now) likewise lacks the ambiguous-elapsed rejection RecordedClimateSensor/Dht11Sensor perform.
findings.recommendation: Align with the climate arc: add an InvalidTiming (or equivalent) state to MoistureSampleState, guard staleAfter and age against maximumUnambiguousDuration in sample(), and have WateringController treat it as an invalid sample.

findings.issue: WateringController::initialize on an already-initialized controller returns HardwareFailure when OutputFault is latched, breaking the group-wide 'repeat initialize returns Ok' idempotence every other type follows. Meanwhile GreenhouseController latches outputFaultLatched_ with no reset() — EnvironmentalStation and many sibling arcs (access_trainer.h:98, museum_case_monitor.h:169, traffic_junction.h:75) expose Status reset() — so the only recovery from a transient pump fault is full shutdown()+initialize() of all four subsystems.
findings.recommendation: Keep initialize idempotent (return Ok; surface the latched fault via snapshot/actuate) and add GreenhouseController::reset()/WateringController::reset() following the sibling reset convention to clear latched output faults deliberately.

findings.issue: EnvironmentalStation::shutdown unconditionally calls sensor_->shutdown() with no initialized_ guard, unlike every sibling in the group (MoistureSensor, WateringController, GreenhouseController, GreenhouseHealthPattern all early-return when not initialized). Destroying a never-initialized station therefore shuts down a sensor another owner may have initialized, and initialize()'s config-invalid path leaves the object in a state where the destructor still pokes the sensor.
findings.recommendation: Add the standard 'if (!initialized_) return;' guard (initialize's own failure path already performs its explicit sensor_->shutdown rollback).

findings.issue: GreenhouseController::shutdown runs watering_->decide(decisionAt_, snapshot_.moisture, false) + actuate() before watering_->shutdown(), but WateringController::shutdown already forces the pump off (pump_->setState(Off) at watering_controller.cpp:71); the preamble replays a decision with a stale decisionAt_ timestamp and can pointlessly latch OutputFault inside a controller being torn down.
findings.recommendation: Drop the decide/actuate preamble and rely on WateringController::shutdown's guaranteed pump-off, which is the documented safety contract of that type.

findings.issue: EnvironmentalStationConfig ships safe member defaults, but GreenhouseConfig is four positional Duration fields with none — every caller writes brace-lists like {Duration(100), Duration(200), Duration(300), Duration(250)} (repeated ~8 times in test_greenhouse_controller.cpp, again in Lesson024) where transposing sampleInterval/staleAfter compiles silently and only fails at initialize(); WateringConfig mixes raw uint16_t permille thresholds with Durations the same way.
findings.recommendation: Give GreenhouseConfig and WateringConfig validated member defaults like EnvironmentalStationConfig so call sites override only what a lesson varies, and so field intent is visible via designated-style member naming at the definition.

result.summary: Audited the greenhouse-climate group (8 type pairs, ~2.6k lines) plus Lessons 013/015/024 and seven test binaries. The arc is generally disciplined (inert construction, idempotent initialize, snapshot pattern), but four issues stand out. Most severe: StatusCode::InvalidArgument is overloaded across three physical meanings, so EnvironmentalStation classifies an out-of-range DHT11 reading as a TimingFault and Lesson015 permanently halts on it. Structurally, MoistureSensor is the only sensor without an abstract seam, forcing the full AnalogInput fake stack into every GreenhouseController consumer; the ClimateSensor freshness policy is copy-pasted across implementations (test fakes already drifted); and Dht11Sensor's transport seam is bypassed by direct pinMode calls. Ceremony findings: GreenhouseController's five-phase per-tick pipeline (vs sibling single update(now, input)), the hand-written init/rollback ladder repeated in every composite and sketch, and GreenhouseHealthPattern living outside the composition while including the whole controller header for one enum. Remaining items are convention drift: missing InvalidTiming/ambiguity handling in MoistureSensor, missing reset() and non-idempotent initialize around latched output faults, an unguarded EnvironmentalStation::shutdown, a redundant decide/actuate shutdown preamble, and positional no-default config structs. Read-only audit; no files modified.

findings.issue: InertCueScheduler cannot be re-initialized after shutdown. initialize() returns ResourceBusy when audit_.initialized() is true, but shutdown() (line 91) deliberately leaves the audit buffer initialized so entries stay readable. So the natural sequence initialize -> shutdown -> initialize permanently fails unless the caller knows to call audit.shutdown() externally, wiping the log. The audit lifecycle is half-owned: initialize() claims the buffer (calls audit_.initialize) but shutdown() does not release it. InertShowSimulator had to grow an ownsAuditSession_ workaround (inert_show_simulator.cpp:91-100) that force-shutdowns the audit on re-init, evidence the seam is broken; a standalone scheduler (Lesson029 pattern) has no such escape.
findings.recommendation: Make audit ownership symmetric: either the scheduler never initializes the audit (require the caller to pass an initialized buffer, dropping the ResourceBusy pre-check) or the scheduler fully owns the session and re-initialize is allowed to reclaim a buffer it previously claimed (track its own session token the way InertShowSimulator does, but inside the scheduler so every consumer benefits).

findings.issue: ConsoleSource is a 10-field positional aggregate that flattens TelemetrySample + ObservationState (sourceId, kind, quality, sequenceState, freshness, value, decimalExponent, packetValidity, observationStatus, present), but nothing bridges the lesson-026 producers (TelemetryPacketCodec, ObservationTracker) to it. Every caller hand-assembles the struct with a brittle positional brace list — Lesson027's fixtureSource() (Lesson027TelemetryConsole.ino:404-421) exists solely to do this. The console arc and the packet arc share vocabulary types but no adapter, so the composition the curriculum implies (packets -> tracker -> console) must be rebuilt by hand at each call site.
findings.recommendation: Add a factory/adapter, e.g. ConsoleSource fromObservation(uint16_t sourceId, const ObservationState&, PacketValidity), or give ConsoleSource a named-field builder, so the packet/tracker arc feeds the console directly.

findings.issue: Three record encoders in this group each hand-roll identical anonymous-namespace text helpers (appendCharacter/appendText/appendUnsigned-or-Decimal, digit-reversal loops), and each exposes a different output convention: InfraredRecordEncoder writes to MutableTextSpan, TelemetryRecordEncoder has MutableTextSpan and StableRecord overloads, CueAuditEncoder takes raw (char*, uint8_t capacity). Same job, three shapes; a fourth encoder will clone the helpers again.
findings.recommendation: Extract a small shared record-writer utility (bounded text appender over MutableTextSpan) and standardize all encoders on the MutableTextSpan + Result<uint16_t> signature; add a StableRecord convenience overload in one place.

findings.issue: The cue-to-channel association is split across two parallel arrays in two config objects the caller must keep index-aligned by hand: InertCueSchedulerConfig.plan.cues (fed to the scheduler) and InertCueChannelMap.channels (fed to the simulator). Lesson030 declares 4 cues in schedulerConfig and separately {{5,2,7,0},4} in cueChannelMap; a count or ordering mismatch is only caught at initialize() as a generic InvalidConfiguration (inert_show_simulator.cpp:86, validMap at :273) with no indication of which row is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Let the show-level config own rows of {cueId, offset, visibleFor, channel} and derive both the scheduler plan and the channel map from it, eliminating the parallel-array invariant.

findings.issue: InertLoadInterlock (policy) and InertLoadPanel (indicators) do not compose in the library; every caller must replay the four-step dance interlock.select(load) -> interlock.update() -> interlock.snapshot().active -> panel.select(active). Lesson023 repeats it in both selectVisibleIntent and showFailClosed; forgetting the panel.select step silently desynchronizes indicators from the interlock decision. The two types are also copy-paste siblings: identical private validLoad() (inert_load_interlock.cpp:103, inert_load_panel.cpp:168) and near-duplicate snapshot structs InertLoadSnapshot{requested,active,status} vs SimulatedLoadSnapshot{active,lastStatus} that differ only in field naming (status vs lastStatus).
findings.recommendation: Provide a composed type (or give InertLoadInterlock an optional panel reference) so select/update propagate to the indicators automatically; share one SimulatedLoad validity helper and unify the snapshot shape.

findings.issue: TelemetryConsoleOperator and TelemetryConsolePresentation each demand the full initialize/shutdown/initialized lifecycle triple, so every sketch adapter re-implements ordered init with rollback and idempotence guards: Lesson027's ConsoleButtons spends ~60 lines wrapping two Buttons and ConsoleEvidence another ~30 wrapping one RgbLed, mostly lifecycle plumbing the library already knows how to do (TelemetryConsoleProject::initialize/rollback and InertLoadPanel::initialize implement the same acquire-with-rollback pattern a third and fourth time).
findings.recommendation: Narrow the interfaces to their domain methods (update/nextPressEvent/acknowledgePressEvent; present) and let the project treat lifecycle via an optional base or a shared multi-child acquire/rollback helper, so sketch adapters shrink to the interesting few lines.

findings.issue: PacketReceiver is exported from Adk.h and tested, but no example or other src type consumes it — the telemetry arc it belongs to (Lesson026) generates packets locally via TelemetryFixtureSchedule instead. Its shape also fights the mental model: the name suggests a radio/receiver component, but it is a one-slot submit/latest/acknowledge mailbox whose update(now) ignores the time argument entirely (packet_receiver.cpp:96-106).
findings.recommendation: Either wire it into the lesson arc it was built for (fixture -> receiver -> codec -> tracker) or remove it; if kept, rename to reflect the latch/mailbox role and drop the no-op time parameter.

findings.issue: Sibling decoders disagree on how to report outcome: TelemetryPacketCodec::decode returns a bare PacketValidity with no Status, while InfraredDecoder::decode (infrared_decoder.h:36) returns Status and stores FrameValidity inside the out-param frame. Same decode-with-validity job, opposite signalling shapes; downstream code (TelemetryEvidenceModel::decide takes validity + status separately) has to carry both conventions.
findings.recommendation: Pick one shape for codec decode across arcs — Status return with validity in the output struct matches the rest of the library — and migrate TelemetryPacketCodec at the next breaking window.

findings.issue: InfraredRecordEncoder's maximum record size (recordCapacity = 80) is hidden in the .cpp, unlike siblings TelemetryRecordEncoder::maximumLength (49) and CueAuditEncoder::maximumLength (96) which expose it. Lesson025 must guess: it hardcodes 'char record[80]' (Lesson025InfraredEvidence.ino:223), a magic number that will silently truncate if the format grows.
findings.recommendation: Expose static constexpr uint8_t maximumLength on InfraredRecordEncoder (matching the sibling convention) and size caller buffers from it.

findings.issue: Lesson demo scaffolding lives in library src/ as first-class components: TelemetryFixtureSchedule hardcodes a 12-second accept/gap/corrupt/silence demo cycle (telemetry_evidence.cpp:102-141) and exists only for Lesson026; RecordedInertObservationSource (inert_channel_assessor.h:59) is consumed only by tests. Both carry the full initialize/shutdown/initialized ceremony of real components, blurring the type-to-component correspondence the library otherwise maintains (types read as hardware or policy).
findings.recommendation: Move fixture/playback types into the example sketch or a fixtures/ area (tests already have tests/fixtures), or at minimum name/namespace them as fixtures so they do not read as shippable components.

findings.issue: InertShowInput advertises a flexible observations pointer + observationCount, but canonicalizeFrame rejects anything except exactly InertChannelAssessor::capacity (8) entries — while the underlying InertChannelAssessor::update happily accepts partial sets (0..capacity). The field shape lies about flexibility, and Lesson030 must maintain a full synthetic 8-channel frame and re-stamp every channel's observedAt on each apply (Lesson030 ino:227-231) purely to satisfy it.
findings.recommendation: Either accept partial frames like the assessor does (treating absent channels as unchanged) or replace the pointer+count pair with a fixed-size array reference so the requirement is expressed in the type.

findings.issue: PanelPumpOutput hardcodes SimulatedLoad::Pump in setState (inert_load_panel.cpp:239): the adapter can only ever represent the pump, and there is no way to expose the fan or heater channels of the same panel as PumpOutput without writing a new class. The generic name and generic constructor (takes just the panel) hide that constraint; setState(On) also silently kicks off whatever other load was active because it routes through panel select semantics.
findings.recommendation: Give PanelPumpOutput a SimulatedLoad constructor parameter naming the load it fronts (validated against None), so one type covers all three channels and the pump-only behavior stops being an invisible special case.

findings.issue: CueAuditBuffer's entire append surface is private behind 'friend struct InertCueScheduler', making the audit log compile-time bound to a single writer. InertShowSimulator holds the same buffer but can only read count(); to get its own fault transitions audited it must route them through the scheduler with a synthetic Fault gate (enterInputFault, inert_show_simulator.cpp:437-450), and show-level events (state changes, digest milestones) cannot be recorded at all.
findings.recommendation: Replace the friend seam with a narrow public append API (or a writer-token/session handle) so composed owners like the simulator can record their own events without impersonating scheduler input.

findings.issue: Frame-validation logic is triplicated across the inert arc: sameOperatorInput (inert_show_simulator.cpp:47) duplicates InertCueScheduler::sameInput (inert_cue_scheduler.cpp:692), validObservation appears verbatim in both inert_show_simulator.cpp:11 and inert_channel_assessor.cpp:9, and canonicalizeFrame re-runs the channel-range/duplicate/future-age checks that assessor_.update immediately re-validates on the same data.
findings.recommendation: Add equality helpers (operator== or a compare function) on CueOperatorInput and InertChannelObservation in their headers, expose one validObservation, and let the simulator trust the assessor's validation instead of pre-duplicating it.

result.summary: Audited the telemetry-ir-show group (14 src pairs, ~5.4k lines) plus consuming sketches (Lessons 023-030) and tests. The group is generally disciplined — consistent initialize/shutdown/initialized/update/snapshot lifecycles, deleted copies, Status-everywhere — but has one real lifecycle defect and several structural seams that push work onto every caller. Most severe: InertCueScheduler cannot be re-initialized after shutdown (initialize demands an uninitialized audit buffer that its own shutdown deliberately leaves initialized; InertShowSimulator carries an ownsAuditSession_ hack to dodge exactly this). Other notable findings: ConsoleSource has no bridge from the packet/tracker arc so callers hand-build a 10-field positional aggregate; three record encoders triplicate identical text-append helpers with three different output signatures; the cue-plan/channel-map parallel arrays make Lesson030 wiring fragile; interlock->panel propagation is caller-owned boilerplate repeated per step in Lesson023; the console project's operator/presentation interfaces force ~90 lines of lifecycle adapter code per sketch; and PacketReceiver is an orphaned, misleadingly named type exported from Adk.h with no consumer. Lower-severity items cover convention drift (decode signalling shapes, hidden vs exposed maximumLength), lesson fixtures shipped as library components, a lying observationCount field, the pump-hardcoded PanelPumpOutput adapter, the friend-locked audit buffer, and triplicated validation helpers.

findings.issue: The dwell-qualified binary state machine (candidate_/candidateSince_/stableSince_/hasCandidate_, activation/deactivation event derivation, stableFor accounting, clearCandidate) is written out five times in this arc: LinearHall::publish (magnetic_observation.cpp:218-285), MagneticContact::update (:349-416), ReflectiveObservationPolicy and BeamObservationPolicy (optical_observation.cpp, 18 candidate/stable sites), and PirObservationPolicy (presence_model.cpp, candidateStarted_/stableStarted_). Each copy re-derives the same edge cases (first-update anchoring, candidate replacement, dwell expiry) independently, and they have already drifted in small ways (MagneticContact sets activationEvent unconditionally on commit; LinearHall guards wasActive).
findings.recommendation: Extract a small shared DwellQualifier value type (raw active flag + now -> qualified active, activation/deactivation events, stableFor) and compose it into all five policies; the polarity-specific classify/reported logic stays in LinearHall.

findings.issue: constexpr halfRange = 0x80000000UL plus a hand-rolled forward-time/duration validity guard is copied into ~35 .cpp anonymous namespaces across the library (magnetic_observation, passage_qualifier, contact_dynamics, presence_model, course_marshal, inertial_observation, acoustic_envelope, ...). The copies are not identical: passage_qualifier.cpp:47 requires a nonzero duration while presence_model.cpp:48 accepts zero, and helper names vary (validForwardTime vs inline comparisons), so the monotonic-time contract is re-decided per file and can silently diverge.
findings.recommendation: Own the contract once in time.h (e.g., TimePoint::isForwardOf(earlier) and Duration::withinPolicyRange()/isPositive()) and delete the per-file copies; each policy then states which variant it means explicitly.

findings.issue: LinearHall and MagneticContact are the only observation policies in arcs 31-45 that own their hardware endpoint (AnalogInput/DigitalInput members, ResourceRegistry constructor). Every later sibling (ContactDynamics, AcousticEnvelope, Reflective/Beam/Pir policies, InertialObservationPolicy) is a pure copied-sample policy explicitly commented as owning no GPIO. The coupling forces downstream consumers to fabricate whole 11-field MagneticObservation aggregates by hand when no hardware exists: Lesson035PassageQualifier.ino:208-222 builds one positionally per fixture frame, and PassageInput carries two full observations per update.
findings.recommendation: Split the qualification policy out of LinearHall/MagneticContact into copied-sample policies mirroring optical_observation.h (Sample in, Observation out), keeping thin hardware wrappers that own the input and feed the policy; fixtures and PassageQualifier then share one honest construction path.

findings.issue: update() return conventions are split inside the group: PassageQualifier::update, LinearHall::update, and MagneticContact::update return void (callers must fish status out of snapshot(), as Lesson035 does with decidedPassage.status), while ContactDynamics, AcousticEnvelope, CalibrationConsole, PercussionSequencer, the optical/PIR policies, PresenceModel, InertialObservationPolicy, and both lesson-44 policies return Status from update. Callers of the arc cannot use one error-handling idiom.
findings.recommendation: Make the three void updates return Status like their siblings (the value is already computed into snapshot_.status); call sites keep working since the result is discardable.

findings.issue: Pure policies disagree on teardown vocabulary: CalibrationConsole and PercussionSequencer expose shutdown() despite owning no hardware (CalibrationConsole::shutdown is a de-initialize that preserves committed values; PercussionSequencer::shutdown wipes state), while every other pure policy in the arc (PassageQualifier, ContactDynamics, AcousticEnvelope, optical/PIR, PresenceModel, InertialObservationPolicy, OrientationPolicy) uses reset() and documents 'owns no GPIO and therefore has no shutdown'. Examples show the cost: Lesson033 stopSafely calls console.shutdown() but Lesson035/038 call qualifier.reset()/envelope.reset() — the caller must remember per type.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one rule (reset() for pure policies, shutdown() only where a physical endpoint is released) and rename CalibrationConsole::shutdown and PercussionSequencer::shutdown accordingly.

findings.issue: CourseMarshal's constructor takes six separate caller-owned storage references (CourseRunStorage, CourseTriggerStorage, CourseTriggerPresenceStorage, CourseReplayFrameStorage, CourseReplayPresenceStorage, CourseReplayEventStorage), each a single-member wrapper struct. Every caller (Lesson042CourseMarshal.ino:38-48, tests) must declare six correctly-role-named globals and pass them in exact positional order; three of the six parameter types are mutually confusable single-record wrappers, and a swapped pair would compile only where types differ.
findings.recommendation: Keep the six small objects (the AVR object-ceiling comment justifies the split) but bundle them behind one CourseMarshalStorage struct containing the six members — or a struct of six references — so construction is one declaration and one argument.

findings.issue: PreparedOrientationEstimate (:58-70) and PreparedBalancePresentation (:151-163) are structurally identical transaction tokens (result_, const Policy* owner_, uint32_t generation_, friend of the policy, private everything) duplicated within one header, and each policy re-implements the same preview/canCommit/commit generation bookkeeping. Any future policy adopting the lesson-44 transaction pattern (later arcs already use preview, e.g. lessons 46/58/59) will copy the token a third time.
findings.recommendation: Introduce one shared Prepared<Result, Policy> template (templates are already accepted — Result<Value> in status.h) or a common PreparedToken base holding owner/generation, and have both policies reuse it.

findings.issue: Four hand-rolled monomorphic optionals (OptionalPirObservation, OptionalBeamObservation, OptionalReflectiveObservation, OptionalTimedRangeEvidence) with identical {bool present; T value;} shape exist solely to build PresenceInput, even though the codebase already accepts class templates (Result<Value> in status.h). Each new evidence source added to PresenceInput will mint another Optional* struct.
findings.recommendation: Replace the quadruplet with a single template <typename T> struct Optional { bool present; T value; }; call sites keep aggregate initialization unchanged.

findings.issue: LoggerConfig and LoggerSnapshot are the only component types in the arc named without their component: every sibling prefixes (PassageQualifierConfig, PercussionSequencerSnapshot, BalanceInstrumentConfig, ...). In the flat adk namespace 'LoggerConfig' claims a generic name for a magnetic-passage-specific shape and reads as a library-wide logging facility; a second logger lesson cannot use the natural name.
findings.recommendation: Rename to MagneticPassageLoggerConfig / MagneticPassageLoggerSnapshot (or PassageLoggerConfig/-Snapshot) to restore type-to-component correspondence.

findings.issue: Config construction is split mid-arc: lessons 31-39 configs carry hand-written constructors that only forward members (JoystickAxisConfig, AnalogJoystickConfig, QuadratureEncoderConfig, CalibrationConsoleConfig, ContactDynamicsConfig, AcousticEnvelopeConfig, PercussionSequencerConfig — all validation still happens in initialize()), while configs from lesson 34 onward in the same files/arc are plain aggregates (LinearHallConfig, MagneticContactConfig, all optical/presence/course/orientation/balance configs). The ceremonial constructors add .cpp definitions and forbid brace/field-order-checked aggregate initialization without buying any invariant; magnetic_observation.h even mixes both styles' neighbors.
findings.recommendation: Drop the member-forwarding config constructors and standardize on aggregate configs (the later-arc convention), keeping validation in initialize() where it already lives.

findings.issue: Loop-cadence and evidence-latch scaffolding is re-implemented per sketch: Lesson039 ships three private utility types (FrameCueGate, Lesson039EvidenceLatch, Lesson039SampleCadence) plus a ReplaySchedule; Lesson042 re-implements ReplaySchedule inline (:51-69); Lessons 035/036 hand-roll the same nextStepAtMs/startedAtMs arithmetic and duration cut-offs. Every consuming sketch repeats fixed-interval scheduling and timed-latch logic the library never offers, with the usual wraparound pitfalls re-decided each time.
findings.recommendation: Promote two tiny utilities into src/ (e.g., adk::Cadence{interval; due(now)} and adk::TimedLatch{duration; trigger/active}) built on TimePoint/Duration, and use them in the examples.

findings.issue: 'Checkpoint' means two unrelated things in adjacent arcs of the same namespace: PassageCheckpoint (passage_ledger.h:20) is a persistence commit marker (generation/count/sequence), while CheckpointId/CheckpointBinding/CheckpointEvent/RecordedCheckpoint (course_marshal.h) are physical course gates. A reader of LoggerSnapshot and CourseRunRecord side by side must hold both meanings; neither type reads unambiguously as its physical or policy referent.
findings.recommendation: Rename the ledger type toward its persistence role (e.g., LedgerCheckpoint or CommitMark), leaving 'checkpoint' to the physical course-gate family.

result.summary: Audited arc-031-045 (16 components in /home/ksh/git/adk/src: analog_joystick, quadrature_encoder, calibration_console, magnetic_observation, magnetic_passage_logger, passage_ledger, passage_qualifier, contact_dynamics, acoustic_envelope, percussion_sequencer, optical_observation, presence_model, course_marshal, inertial_observation, orientation_presentation, balance_table_instrument) plus their Lesson031-045 sketches and tests. The arc's core copied-sample-policy shape is sound and consistently testable, but two high-severity duplication seams dominate: the dwell/candidate qualification state machine is hand-copied five times (magnetic, optical x2, PIR, contact), and the halfRange forward-time guard is copied into ~35 translation units with semantic variants. Mid-severity findings are convention drift the arc itself created and then abandoned: the magnetic devices still own hardware unlike every later observation policy, update() returns void in three types and Status everywhere else, pure policies split between shutdown() and reset(), CourseMarshal demands six positional storage references, and the lesson-44 Prepared transaction token is duplicated within one header. Low-severity items cover hand-rolled Optional quadruplets, generic LoggerConfig naming, mixed config-constructor styles, per-sketch cadence/latch re-implementation, and the double meaning of 'checkpoint'. No formatting or style-checker issues reported; no files were modified (read-only lane; no journal writes per delegated-lane posture).

findings.issue: The external-durable-commit protocol is implemented twice as parallel unshared type triads: EnrollmentCandidate/IdentityImageView/IdentityDurableCommitEvidence (registry) and DurableAuditCandidate/AuditRecordView/AuditDurableCommitEvidence (carousel), with matching preview/export/acknowledge method triads. The evidence structs are field-for-field identical (owner, generation, operationId, slot, reconciled view, synchronized, rereadValidated, durableStatus). Worse, callers must hand-copy owner/generation/operationId/slot out of the candidate into the evidence struct even though the candidate is passed alongside it and the object cross-validates the echo (examples/Lesson049...ino:296-306 and Lesson051...ino:356-366 are byte-identical ceremonies).
findings.recommendation: Extract one shared durable-slot-commit seam (common Candidate/RecordView/CommitEvidence structs or a small DurableSlotJournal component both types compose), and drop the echoed identity fields from the evidence struct so callers only supply what they actually learned (reconciled view, synchronized, rereadValidated, durableStatus).

findings.issue: Each preview struct privately mirrors the owning policy's entire mutable state field-by-field (HomingPreview repeats 14 of BoundedHomingPolicy's members, including five bitfields), and commit() copies every field back individually (bounded_homing_policy.cpp:606-629, bounded_stepper_sequence.cpp:383-400). Adding one state field requires touching four sites per policy across three policies; a missed line in commit silently drops committed state with no compiler help.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a nested State struct per policy that both the policy and its preview embed; preview computes a State, commit becomes 'state_ = candidate.state_; ++generation_;'. This collapses the triplicated field lists and makes the copy-back drift-proof.

findings.issue: InertEscapeConsole composes its children only through friendship into their private preflight/apply internals (preflightUpdate/applyPreparedUpdate/preparedSnapshot/preparedEvidence, preflightProjectUpdate/applyPreparedUpdate/invalidatePreparedCandidates). The two-phase all-or-nothing update contract the composite depends on is not part of either child's public interface, and preflightProjectUpdate takes 13 positional parameters (fault_aware_operator_panel.h:311-323) despite a ProjectUpdateView struct existing right below it.
findings.recommendation: Promote the preflight/apply pair to a public, documented two-phase API on both children (matching the arc's preview/canCommit/commit idiom) and pass ProjectUpdateView instead of 13 positional arguments; delete the friend declarations.

findings.issue: ClueConstraintModel::preflightUpdate is declared const but stores the whole prepared evaluation in ten mutable members (preparationActive_, preparedObservations_[12], preparedNow_, preparedMask_, prepared rule masks/dispositions) and even increments preparationGeneration_ inside a const call; the PreparedUpdate out-param is mostly a token pointing back at hidden state, so only one preparation can exist and any interleaved preflight silently invalidates the first. Its sibling FaultAwareOperatorPanel does the same job correctly: PreparedUpdate carries the full proposed state and the panel has no mutable members.
findings.recommendation: Move the prepared evaluation into PreparedUpdate itself (as FaultAwareOperatorPanel::PreparedUpdate does), delete the mutable cache, and make preflightUpdate genuinely const.

findings.issue: Every consumer of the preview/canCommit/commit policies re-implements the same tri-call plus status-merge, and each invents a different status for 'preview ok but canCommit false': Lesson050 returns InternalInvariant, Lesson046 returns InvalidArgument, Lesson047 returns the preview status, kinetic_sculpture.cpp maps it to InvalidArgument or BoundRejected. The ambiguity exists because preview can succeed while canCommit fails and the object never names that outcome.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-shot convenience (e.g. Status apply(TimePoint, const Command&)) that performs preview+canCommit+commit with a canonical status for the stale-candidate case, keeping the three-step API for callers that genuinely need two-phase control.

findings.issue: OperatorSourceIdentity and ClueSourceIdentity are field-for-field identical structs ({uint16 sourceId, uint16 configurationRevision, uint32 sessionEpoch}) defined by two components that are composed together in lesson 057, forcing the sketch to write duplicate hash helpers hashClueSource/hashOperatorSource (Lesson057...ino:237-249). InteractionSource and CarouselSource likewise share the exact {kind, sourceId, configurationRevision} shape with only the kind enum differing.
findings.recommendation: Define one shared SourceIdentity struct (and one kinded variant parameterized by the kind enum, or a plain shared struct plus per-arc kind field) in a common evidence header; alias per arc if distinct names aid teaching.

findings.issue: The arc uses three transactional idioms and two preview-opacity models. Lessons 046/047/050: Status preview(out-param) + canCommit + commit with previews whose fields are private behind friend. Lesson 053: Result<Preview> prepare + commit(preview, now). Lessons 054/056/057: Result<Preview> prepare + commit smuggled through update()-input flags (commitPresent/auditAcknowledgePresent). The later previews expose owner/ownerToken and all validation fields publicly (const void* owner, uintptr_t ownerToken), so callers can forge or mutate tokens the earlier design deliberately sealed.
findings.recommendation: Pick one transactional shape (Result<Preview> prepare + canCommit + commit is the most ergonomic) and one opacity rule (private fields + friend, as in 046-050) and converge the IR/panel/console types toward it in their next revision.

findings.issue: Four types in the arc (InertPartsCarousel, CapturedIrEvidence, KnownIrEmissionPolicy, InertIrTranslator) omit the bool initialized() accessor that the other eight group members and 26 headers library-wide expose, forcing callers to infer readiness from snapshot().status; LocalIdentityRegistry is also the only type in the group whose reset() returns Status while siblings return void.
findings.recommendation: Add initialized() to the four types; align reset() signatures within the arc (or document why registry reset can fail while carousel reset cannot).

findings.issue: The update-input structs are hand-rolled optionals (bool xPresent + payload pairs), and update() rejects inputs whose absent payloads are not zero-canonical (e.g. !clueUpdatePresent && !emptyClueUpdate(...) returns InvalidArgument), so every caller must fully zero 16-field structs before use; tests and sketches each grow their own emptyInput()/loadEnvelope() builders with fragile positional brace-init (tests/test_fault_aware_operator_panel.cpp:133-151, Lesson057 loadEnvelope).
findings.recommendation: Give the input structs default member initializers producing the canonical empty value (so 'Input in; in.now = ...;' is valid), or provide a static empty(now) factory on each input type, and consider small setClue/setStop/setControl helpers that set flag and payload together.

findings.issue: Directional evidence arrives as a bundled DirectionalEvidence envelope (source, observedAt, sequence, payload, status) but contact evidence is passed as three loose arguments (contactSource, contactSequence, ContactSample), because ContactSample predates the evidence-envelope convention. The asymmetry propagates: SculptureInput flattens touchSource/touchSequence/touchSample plus six loose stop* fields (stopSource/stopObservedAt/stopSequence/stopActive/stopQuality/stopStatus) that are exactly the shape of the existing CopiedBinaryEvidence envelope.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a ContactEvidence envelope (source, observedAt, sequence, sample payload, status) and a binary-stop envelope for SculptureInput, so every copied input reads as one evidence record like DirectionalEvidence does.
