findings.issue: KineticLightSculpture copies minimumLogicalPosition/maximumLogicalPosition out of the StepperSequenceConfig at construction and re-implements endpoint bounds-checking before preview, then separately maps a !canCommit preview to BoundRejected — two authorities for the same travel limit that can drift. BoundedHomingPolicy grew excursionBounds() for exactly this consumer need, but BoundedStepperSequence exposes no bounds accessor.
findings.recommendation: Expose the positional bounds on BoundedStepperSequence (mirroring BoundedHomingPolicy::excursionBounds) or have preview report a distinct bound-rejection disposition, and delete the sculpture's cached copies and duplicate check.

findings.issue: MicrosecondTimePoint/MicrosecondDuration live in pulse_input.h, the IR pulse-capture component header, so the escape-room arc (clue model, operator panel, console) includes an IR input component solely for time types; time.h holds only the millisecond types. The dependency graph claims the escape console is built on pulse capture, which fights the component mental model.
findings.recommendation: Move MicrosecondTimePoint/MicrosecondDuration into time.h (or a microsecond_time.h) and have pulse_input.h include it.

findings.issue: carousel_evidence.h and CarouselSource/CarouselSourceKind name shared evidence types after one downstream consumer: LocalIdentityRegistry (lesson 049) and BoundedHomingPolicy (lesson 050) both depend on them before the carousel exists, so a homing policy's stop-switch evidence is 'CarouselSource {SyntheticStop,...}'. LocalIdentity/IdentityEvidence are likewise registry concepts housed under the carousel banner, and registry sizing constants (maximumCarouselBins) sit in local_identity_registry.h:11.
findings.recommendation: Rename the header/types to arc-neutral evidence vocabulary (e.g. copied_evidence.h, CopiedSource) or split identity types into an identity_evidence.h owned by the registry, and move maximumCarouselBins next to the carousel.

findings.issue: InertPartsCarousel stores 'const CarouselConfig* config_' pointing at the caller's config object, while every sibling in the group (BoundedHomingPolicy, LocalIdentityRegistry, KnownIrEmissionPolicy, InertIrTranslator, FaultAwareOperatorPanel) copies its config by value; a caller constructing the carousel from a temporary or stack config that goes out of scope gets a dangling config with no diagnostic, and its 9-parameter raw-buffer constructor (pointer/extent/stride/capacity) contrasts with the arc's own IrPulseStorage descriptor pattern.
findings.recommendation: Copy the config by value like its siblings (it is ~70 bytes, comparable to what siblings copy), or document the lifetime contract loudly; bundle the audit-slot buffer parameters into a storage descriptor struct like IrPulseStorage.

result.summary: Audited arc-046-057 (13 src groups, ~12k lines) plus their lesson sketches and tests. The arc is disciplined about inert/copied-evidence boundaries, but object design shows three systemic problems. (1) Duplicated structure: the external-durable-commit protocol exists twice as unshared parallel type triads in LocalIdentityRegistry and InertPartsCarousel, with callers forced to echo candidate identity fields back in the evidence struct; preview structs in the 046/047/050 policies each mirror their policy's whole private state field-by-field with hand-written commit copy-back; and two pairs of source-identity structs are field-for-field identical, forcing Lesson057 to write duplicate hash helpers. (2) Missing seams: InertEscapeConsole composes its children via friendship into private preflight/apply internals (including a 13-positional-argument private call), ClueConstraintModel launders its entire preparation state through mutable members inside a const preflight while its sibling panel does the same job cleanly via the out-param, and KineticLightSculpture duplicates stepper travel bounds because BoundedStepperSequence exposes no bounds accessor. (3) Convention drift and caller ceremony: three transactional idioms and two preview-opacity models coexist in one arc, four types omit the arc-standard initialized() accessor, hand-rolled bool-present optional input structs require zero-canonicalized absent payloads so every consumer builds its own emptyInput helpers, and the preview/canCommit/commit tri-call is repeated at every call site with each caller inventing a different status for the stale-candidate case. Fourteen findings reported, ranked most severe first; no files were modified.

findings.issue: The newer descriptors/configs are bare aggregates with 20-27 positional fields dominated by adjacent uint32_t/uint16_t members (SmallIndicatorDescriptor has 27, LowSideDriverDescriptor 20 plus a nested 16-field LowSideCurrentBudget). Every call site brace-initializes them positionally (examples/Lesson080SmallIndicatorSemantics.ino:52-99, tests/small_indicator_semantics_policy_test.cpp:19-48); a transposed pair of integers compiles silently and only fails, if at all, at validate-time. This drifts from the arc's own earlier convention: MultiplexedDigitConfig and Max7219PresentationConfig (058/059) have narrow constructors with defaults.
findings.recommendation: Give the wide descriptors/configs constructors (or grouped sub-structs like identity/budget/timing built from small constructors) so field order errors cannot compile, matching the 058/059 config style. At minimum, group the flat integer runs into named sub-structs so brace-init is chunked and self-checking.

findings.issue: Seven sibling structs (LowSideDriveRequest, LowSideControl, LowSideDriveIntent, SmallIndicatorSemanticRequest, SmallIndicatorObservation, SmallIndicatorControl, SmallIndicatorSemanticResult) each re-declare the same correlation header (lifecycleGeneration, sessionId, runId, stepId, requestId, sourceId, sourceConfigurationRevision, sequence, observedAt, producerStatus). Callers must build three parallel structs with matching values per step (Lesson080 observeCopiedEvidence(), lines 257-321, repeats sessionId/runId/stepId/requestId across drive, request and observation), and must first round-trip snapshot() just to recover lifecycleGeneration to stamp into each one.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared SessionCorrelation/EvidenceProvenance struct embedded in each evidence type so callers fill it once and reuse it; have beginSession return (or output) the lifecycleGeneration so callers do not fish it from a snapshot.

findings.issue: MuseumCaseConfig spells out four copies of the expected-producer triplet (expectedXSourceId, expectedXConfigurationRevision, expectedXCalibrationRevision) plus four maximumXAge fields as 16 flat members; the same 'expected identity' concept is re-declared ad hoc in ThermalMapperConfig, OneWireTransactionConfig, and ModuleBenchConfig. The desk arc already invented the right seam (TimingDeskControlIdentity) but nothing else reuses it, and its sourceId is uint16_t while every other identity uses uint8_t, so the concept cannot converge.
findings.recommendation: Introduce one ExpectedProducerIdentity {sourceId, configurationRevision, calibrationRevision, maximumAge} value type with a fixed sourceId width and use it in MuseumCaseConfig (liquid/thermistor/digitalTemperature/radiant/reed/acknowledge) and the other configs; this collapses ~20 fields and makes the museum config readable as six producers.

findings.issue: Three hash/checksum algorithms are re-implemented privately at least eight times across this arc (and three more times in earlier arcs). These digests are identity-bearing: receipts and records are compared against them across producer/consumer boundaries, so a divergent private copy (wrong init value, missing final xor) would silently break cross-object verification rather than fail a compile.
findings.recommendation: Add a small shared header (e.g. src/digest.h) with Fnv1a32, Crc16Ccitt, and Crc32 accumulator types and delete the per-file anonymous-namespace copies; keep the domain-prefix convention as a constructor argument as module_characterization_digest.cpp already does.
findings.where: src/dual_display_timing_desk.cpp:83-136 (FNV-1a also privately copied in museum_case_monitor.cpp, thermal_gradient_mapper.cpp; CRC16-CCITT copied in inertial_record.cpp:226, module_characterization_record.cpp:45, qualified_motion_recorder.cpp:391; CRC32 copied in module_characterization_digest.cpp and bounded_low_side_driver_policy.cpp:103-118)

findings.issue: Lifecycle signatures drift arbitrarily inside the arc: initialize is () in 059/061/062/065/079/080 but (TimePoint) in 058/060/063/066/068/071; reset returns void in 058-062 but Status in 063/066/068/069/071/072/079/080; shutdown is void in 058/059/060/079/080, Status in 063/066, Status(TimePoint) in 068/069/071/072; beginSession puts now first (071/072) but last (080: sessionId, runId, startedAt) or omits it (079). None of these differences encode a real behavioral difference, so callers must re-learn the ceremony per lesson.
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical lifecycle contract (suggest: Status initialize(TimePoint), Status reset(TimePoint), Status shutdown(TimePoint), beginSession(TimePoint, ids...)) and align new types to it; document it as the arc convention so 081+ stops drifting.
findings.where: src/museum_case_monitor.h:168-172 vs src/multiplexed_digit_policy.h:129-131 vs src/bounded_low_side_driver_policy.h:163-173 vs src/module_characterization.h:146-156

findings.issue: The terminal read accessor has three names and two shapes within this one arc: `Snapshot snapshot() const` by value (058, 059, 060, 061, 062, 063, 079, 080), `Status snapshot(Snapshot&) const` out-param (064, 065, 066), `Status evidence(Evidence&) const` (068, 071), and `Status result(Result&) const` (069, 072). Consumers switching between siblings must relearn both the name and the error-handling shape for the same operation.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on one accessor name and shape (by-value snapshot() matches the pre-058 library baseline: bounded_homing_policy.h:138, fault_aware_operator_panel.h:255); reserve out-param+Status only where a not-yet-available state is meaningful, and use one name for it.

findings.issue: DigitFrameReceipt and MatrixFrameReceipt are field-for-field identical except reportedFrame's type (MultiplexedDigitFrame vs Max7219Frame). The duplication propagates to callers: Lesson060's copiedDigitReceipt() and copiedMatrixReceipt() (lines 255-283) are near-identical functions, and the desk carries parallel digit*/matrix* member and result fields for each.
findings.recommendation: Factor a common FrameReceiptHeader (ownerToken, lifecycleGeneration, configurationRevision, requested/acceptedGeneration, reportedDigest, observedAt, status, blankRequestAccepted) embedded by both receipts, so callers can fill the header with one shared helper and only the frame payload differs.

findings.issue: MuseumAuditReceipt re-declares all 15 fields of MuseumAuditIntent (plus accepted/status/minus issuedAt), and receipt matching is a hand-written 15-clause field comparison in receiptMatchesIntent. Any field added to the intent must be manually mirrored in the receipt struct, the sketch that echoes it, and the comparison, with silent drift if one site is missed.
findings.recommendation: Embed the intent in the receipt (`MuseumAuditIntent intent; bool accepted; Status status;`) so the echo is structural and matching reduces to comparing one embedded struct via a single equality helper.

findings.issue: ModuleCharacterizationRecord flattens all 18 fields of ModuleThresholdDescriptor into itself instead of embedding the struct, so the bench copies descriptor fields one-by-one when building the record and the codec re-lists them again. A descriptor field addition requires coordinated edits in the descriptor, the record struct, the bench copy, and both codec directions.
findings.recommendation: Embed `ModuleThresholdDescriptor descriptor;` in ModuleCharacterizationRecord (the codec can still serialize members individually), eliminating the field-by-field copy in the bench and halving the places a descriptor change must touch.

findings.issue: SmallIndicatorSemanticsPolicy::apply takes three loose evidence structs plus TimePoint in fourth position plus an out-param, abandoning the envelope convention every other multi-input coordinator in the arc uses (DualDisplayEnvelope, MuseumCaseEnvelope, ThermalMapperEnvelope all bundle `now` with the copied evidence). The odd time-parameter position also invites swapping it relative to sibling policies where now comes first.
findings.recommendation: Introduce SmallIndicatorEnvelope {now, drive, request, observation} and make apply(envelope, result&), matching the 060/063/066 coordinator shape.

findings.issue: SmallIndicatorReason flattens LowSideDriveReason into prefixed duplicates (DriverBudgetExceeded, DriverFlybackMissing, DriverSequenceDiscontinuity, ...) plus a hand-maintained switch translating one enum to the other that returns InvalidArgument on any new driver reason. Every future LowSideDriveReason addition forces a parallel enum value and switch case here.
findings.recommendation: Carry the upstream reason verbatim in the result (e.g. `LowSideDriveReason driveReason;` alongside a collapsed local reason like DriverRejected), deleting the prefixed duplicates and the translation switch.

findings.issue: MultiplexedDigitPreview and Max7219PresentationPreview are structurally identical opaque tokens (owner pointer, lifecycleGeneration, baseFrameGeneration, frame) supporting an identical preview/canCommit/commit trio implemented twice; a third preview-committing display policy would mint a third copy.
findings.recommendation: Extract a small shared FramePreview<Policy, Frame> template (or a common base holding owner/lifecycle/baseGeneration) and shared commit-eligibility logic, keeping the per-policy frame validation separate.

findings.issue: InertialQualificationReason declares two aliases for SequenceDiscontinuity (`Disordered` and `SequenceGap`) that no code in src/, tests/, or examples/ references; three names for one value invite divergent usage and defeat exhaustive-switch reasoning.
findings.recommendation: Delete the unused aliases (or, if they preserve a published ABI meaning, comment why they exist).

findings.issue: The same header mixes two spellings of the part identity: the policy is Qualified18B20ProbeSetPolicy (capital B, no Ds) while every companion type is QualifiedDs18b20Probe/QualifiedDs18b20Snapshot/QualifiedDs18b20SetConfig/Ds18b20*, so a grep for either convention misses half the family and the policy name reads as a different component from its own snapshot type.
findings.recommendation: Rename the policy to QualifiedDs18b20ProbeSetPolicy (with the file rename tracked for a suitable release point) so the whole family shares the Ds18b20 stem.

result.summary: Audited the arc-058-080 group (19 src pairs, ~17k lines) plus consuming lessons 058-080 sketches and tests. The objects are individually disciplined (deleted copies, noexcept, inert-policy separation), but the arc accumulated three systemic costs. (1) Construction: the newer descriptors/configs regressed from the 058/059 constructor style to 20-27-field positional aggregates that every sketch and test brace-initializes blind, and identity/correlation headers (lifecycleGeneration/sessionId/runId/stepId/requestId/sourceId/revision) are re-declared in seven sibling structs, forcing callers to build parallel copies and round-trip snapshot() for the lifecycle generation. (2) Missing seams: expected-producer identity triplets, frame receipts, audit intent/receipt echoes, the characterization record's flattened descriptor, and three checksum algorithms are each duplicated field-by-field or file-by-file instead of shared (FNV-1a alone has six private copies). (3) Convention drift: initialize/reset/shutdown signatures, time-parameter position, envelope-vs-loose-arg update, and the terminal accessor (snapshot by value vs snapshot/evidence/result out-params) vary lesson-to-lesson with no behavioral justification. 14 findings reported, ranked; the highest-leverage fixes are constructors/sub-structs for the wide aggregates, a shared correlation/identity struct, and a shared digest header.

findings.issue: Three untracked lesson-081 headers are declaration-only orphans: no .cpp defines InertComponentQualificationBench's methods or the digest functions, none of the three is included from src/Adk.h, and no test, example, or probe consumes them. The bench also silently drops two established conventions: it is the only stateful type in src/ that does not delete copy/move, and its prepareRecord takes a raw `uint8_t* image, size_t imageSize` where the direct sibling bench (inert_module_characterization_bench.h:103) takes a typed ModuleCharacterizationRecordImage&.
findings.recommendation: Before lesson 081 lands: add the .cpp implementations and Adk.h entries (or remove the scaffolding until they exist), delete copy/move like every other stateful type, and take a typed RecordImage struct in prepareRecord to match the 072 bench.

findings.issue: The same 8-10 field evidence-identity header (lifecycleGeneration, sessionId, runId, stepId, requestId/controlId, sourceId, sourceConfigurationRevision, sequence, observedAt, producerStatus) is copy-pasted into ~10 sibling structs across lessons 079-081, with inconsistent field order even within one file: LowSideDriveRequest puts lifecycleGeneration 9th (line 106) while LowSideControl puts it 1st (line 115), and SmallIndicatorSemanticRequest renames `sequence` to `policySequence`/`requestSequence`. Callers fill all of it positionally (examples/Lesson080SmallIndicatorSemantics.ino:268-319 rebuilds three structs by hand every step), so one transposed integer compiles and silently corrupts identity.
findings.recommendation: Extract a shared adk::EvidenceHeader (or SessionIdentity) struct embedded first in every request/observation/control/result struct, and have the policy stamp the session-scoped fields itself after beginSession so callers supply only the per-event fields.

findings.issue: shutdown has three shapes across arcs: `void shutdown()` (early components and the two newest arcs 079/080), `Status shutdown(TimePoint now)` (lessons 63-72: module_characterization, museum_case_monitor, thermal_gradient_mapper, qualified_motion_recorder, inertial_record_qualification, inert_module_characterization_bench), and `Status shutdown(now, OneWireStepIntent& releaseIntent)` (one_wire_transaction_policy.h:195). The library flip-flopped: void, then Status(TimePoint), then back to void, so callers cannot learn one teardown idiom.
findings.recommendation: Converge on `void shutdown() noexcept` with the terminal disposition captured in the snapshot/evidence struct — the direction lessons 079/080 already took — and migrate the 63-72 arc when next touched; shutdown as a safe-state guarantee should not be fallible.

findings.issue: The published-state accessor has four spellings for one concept: `X snapshot() const` by value (majority, ~40 types), `Status snapshot(X&) const` out-param (one_wire_transaction_policy, qualified_18b20_probe_set_policy, thermal_gradient_mapper), `Status evidence(X&) const` (module_characterization), and `Status result(X&) const` (072 bench). Consumers of any two policies must learn different read idioms and different failure semantics for what is a non-fallible copy of cached state.
findings.recommendation: Converge on the value-returning `Snapshot snapshot() const noexcept`; a snapshot of already-cached state cannot fail, so the Status-out-param variants add ceremony with no information. Keep a separate named accessor only when it is genuinely gated (e.g. completedEvidence).

findings.issue: SmallIndicatorDescriptor has 24 positional fields (14 of them undifferentiated uint16/uint32 provenance ids) and LowSideDriverDescriptor has 18 plus a 16-field nested budget; every caller builds them as brace aggregates (tests/small_indicator_semantics_policy_test.cpp:20-48, Lesson080 ino:52-99). Inserting one field silently re-maps every existing literal to the wrong meaning with no compiler diagnostic, and the identity/provenance block (schemaRevision, specimenFamilyReference, specimenReference, specimenRevision, electricalEvidenceRevision, sourcePacketDigest, configurationId, configurationRevision) is itself duplicated verbatim between the two descriptors.
findings.recommendation: Factor the shared provenance block into one reusable struct (e.g. adk::SpecimenProvenance) so descriptors become 3-4 grouped sub-aggregates, which both deduplicates the sibling descriptors and makes positional literals locally checkable.

findings.issue: Two competing identity regimes coexist: the ownerToken claim model (lessons ~52-66: max7219_presentation_policy, fault_aware_operator_panel, inert_escape_console, dual_display_timing_desk, multiplexed_digit_policy, clue_constraint_model, thermal_gradient_mapper, one_wire) and the sessionId/runId/stepId session model (lessons 067+). Worse, ownerToken's type itself drifts: uintptr_t in fault_aware_operator_panel.h:162 vs uint32_t in max7219_presentation_policy.h:41 and one_wire_transaction_policy.h:65, so the same concept is not even portably comparable across the arc.
findings.recommendation: Converge on the sessionId/runId model for new work and declare it in a shared header; where ownerToken remains, fix it to one type (uint32_t, matching the majority) so composite projects can correlate identities across policies.

findings.issue: Session start has three signatures: `begin(now, request, intent&)` (one_wire), `beginSession(TimePoint now, sessionId, runId)` with time first (module_characterization, 072 bench takes an envelope instead of runId), and `beginSession(sessionId, runId[, startedAt])` with time last or absent (079 omits time, 080/081 append startedAt). No type has endSession; sessions end implicitly through reset/cancel/shutdown, which each arc encodes differently.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on one `Status beginSession(...)` signature (ids plus explicit start TimePoint, in one fixed parameter order) and document that reset is the sole session terminator, so the asymmetry is a stated convention rather than accidental drift.

findings.issue: TimePoint threading is inconsistent across arcs: lessons 63-72 pass `now` as the first parameter of every lifecycle call including initialize/reset/shutdown; lessons 079/080 dropped it from lifecycle calls but bury it mid-signature in apply (`apply(drive, request, observation, now, result)`); 079 splits expiry evaluation into a separate `update(now, intent&)` while 080 folds it into apply; one_wire uses MicrosecondTimePoint first everywhere. Callers composing the 079 driver with the 080 indicator (the shipped Lesson080 pairing) must juggle both shapes in one loop.
findings.recommendation: Fix one rule — `now` is always the first parameter of any time-dependent operation, and pure lifecycle ops (initialize/reset/shutdown) never take it — and apply it to the next arc; the 079/080 pair should agree before 081 freezes their combined envelope.

findings.issue: update() has four return conventions: void (button, analog_input, digital_input, piezo_sounder, magnetic_observation, passage_qualifier), Status (majority), Result<T> (only dual_display_timing_desk and telemetry_evidence in the whole library), and a raw observation struct (threshold_input). Result<T> exists in status.h but is used by exactly two types, so it reads as an abandoned experiment; relatedly the embedded status field is named `status` in the 63-72 evidence structs (ModuleCharacterizationEvidence:131, OneWireTransactionSnapshot, ModuleBenchResult) but `producerStatus` in 079/080 structs.
findings.recommendation: Converge on `Status update(...)` with results read via snapshot(); either adopt Result<T> library-wide or retire it, and pick one name (producerStatus for upstream status, status for own terminal status) and use it consistently.

findings.issue: Composite sketches hand-write a growing failure-unwind pyramid: each component's initialize() failure must shut down every previously initialized sibling in reverse order (lines 118-141), and the same reverse list is repeated again for normal teardown (lines 361-364). Every multi-component lesson repeats this pattern; the library offers no ordered bring-up/tear-down helper even though it already has composite controllers (EnvironmentalStation, GreenhouseController) that solve exactly this internally.
findings.recommendation: Provide a small ordered-initialization helper (e.g. an adk::Startup that records initialized components and unwinds in reverse on failure or shutdown), or extend the composite-controller pattern so sketches own at most one initialize/shutdown pair.

findings.issue: Among pure-logic (no-hardware) policies, the observation arc (contact_dynamics, acoustic_envelope, optical_observation, orientation_presentation, presence_model, pulse_input, ultrasonic_ranger, threshold_input) exposes only initialize/reset, while equally inert later policies (clue_constraint_model, known_ir_emission_policy, small_indicator_semantics_policy) add shutdown() plus terminal Shutdown enum states. The presence of shutdown no longer signals hardware ownership, which was its original meaning in the component arc.
findings.recommendation: Decide what shutdown means for inert policies (terminal evidence state vs hardware release) and apply it uniformly; if terminal-state modeling is the convention going forward, note it in the header comment and stop omitting shutdown in new observation-style types.

findings.issue: snapshot() frequently returns types whose names contradict the snapshot mental model: LowSideDriveIntent (bounded_low_side_driver_policy), MuseumCaseIntent (museum_case_monitor), SmallIndicatorSemanticResult, ContactObservation, CourseStartEvent — an 'Intent' returned from 'snapshot' reads as a command to execute, not published state, while genuinely snapshot-named types (KeypadSnapshot, CarouselSnapshot, etc.) coexist in the same library.
findings.recommendation: Align accessor and type: either name the returned struct *Snapshot (state read) or name the accessor for what it yields (e.g. intent() when the value is a command the caller is expected to act on), so the physical read-vs-drive distinction survives at call sites.

findings.issue: Digest free-function naming drifts within the qualification arcs: 079 exports lowSideDriverDescriptorIdentityDigest (with 'Identity'), while the 080/081 family exports smallIndicatorDescriptorDigest and componentQualification*EvidenceDigest (without), and 080's descriptor field expectedDriverDescriptorIdentityDigest bakes the 079 spelling into a cross-arc contract, making the inconsistency permanent once frozen.
findings.recommendation: Pick one form (descriptor digest vs descriptor identity digest) before the lesson-081 digest domains are frozen, since the CRC domain tags and field names become schema once published.

findings.issue: signed_axis_mapping.h is a tracked, committed header (consumed by inertial_record_qualification.h and orientation_presentation.h) but is the only committed header absent from the Adk.h umbrella, so sketches including <Adk.h> get SignedAxisMapping only transitively and would break if either consumer dropped the include.
findings.recommendation: Add #include "signed_axis_mapping.h" to src/Adk.h to restore the every-header-in-the-umbrella invariant the other 119 headers follow.

result.summary: Audited all ~120 src/ headers plus consuming examples and tests for cross-cutting lifecycle, Status, identity, and umbrella conventions. The library has four distinguishable convention eras: early hardware components (ResourceRegistry ctor, Status initialize / void shutdown / update(now)), the observation arc (initialize/reset only, value snapshot), the ownerToken console arc (~lessons 52-66, Status shutdown(TimePoint), out-param snapshot/evidence, ownerToken identity with even its integer type drifting uintptr_t vs uint32_t), and the session/evidence arc (67-081, sessionId/runId/stepId, beginSession/apply/cancel, value snapshot, void shutdown again). The most severe issues are the three declaration-only, un-umbrellaed lesson-081 scaffolding headers (which also drop the deleted-copy/move and typed-record conventions), and the copy-pasted 8-10 field evidence-identity header re-declared with inconsistent field order across ~10 structs that every caller fills positionally. Convergence recommendation: adopt the lesson-079/080 policy shape as the library-wide convention — descriptor-in-constructor with a free validate function, Status initialize()/reset(), void shutdown(), beginSession(sessionId, runId, startedAt), Status apply(..., Out&), value-returning snapshot() const, deleted copy/move — augmented with a shared EvidenceHeader/SpecimenProvenance struct and a fixed now-first parameter rule, and migrate the 63-72 Status-shutdown/out-param-snapshot arc opportunistically. Call-site ergonomics need two library-owned fixes: policies should stamp session-scoped identity fields themselves after beginSession, and composite sketches need an ordered bring-up/unwind helper to eliminate the reverse-shutdown pyramid every multi-component example repeats.

findings.issue: There is no single obvious first click. findings.recommendation: Pick one funnel: landing primary CTA -> start/ ('Set up and run Lesson 001'), secondary -> course/ ('See the course map'), tertiary -> safety/. Make course.md the only 'Open the course' target (it should link lessons/index.md as its directory). End start.md with a single prominent 'Next: Lesson 001' link so the learner path is landing -> start -> 001.

result.summary: Audited README.md (landing source; staged verbatim as index.md by scripts/site), mkdocs.yml, site/pages/{start,course,components,about,api-supported,safety,build,determinism}.md, site/pages/lessons/index.md, site/pages/projects/*, and scripts/check_site.py gates. Diagnosis: the site does not flow because (1) there is no single entry path -- four equal landing CTAs, with 'Open the course' pointing at the raw 81-row lesson directory while the nav's Course section leads with a different page (course map); (2) the landing leads with a 59-line per-lesson boundary blockquote that buries the pitch; (3) the same boundary/status claims are maintained in four near-verbatim copies (README, about.md, course.md, lessons/index.md) and are already contradicting themselves -- lessons/index.md line 127 still lists published Lesson 080 as planned; (4) three overlapping full-course tables (README arcs+per-lesson mix, course.md status grid, lessons/index directory) give readers the same list three times with no declared authority; (5) nav order ignores audience -- Safety (a landing CTA) is buried under section six, five non-Mega Research pages sit above it, docs/CLI.md sits inside Course, and 'Components' vs 'Component catalog' duplicate; (6) orphans: site/pages/projects/cadence.md (zero inbound links, stale at Lesson 033, duplicating the nav'd docs/projects/component_project_cadence.md) and usb3-matrix.md (reachable only from one line deep in api-supported.md); (7) mkdocs.yml hard-pins 'Current lesson — 080', a per-publication manual edit that check_site.py does not gate. Proposed IA -- Nav: Home; Learn (Start here, Course map, Lessons, Safety); Reference (Supported API, Components, Determinism, Architecture); Contribute (Build locally, Command-line workflow, Development, Testing, Packaging, PDF policy); Plan (Curriculum, Projects, Roadmap, Work queue, Complete-kit cadence); Research (mesh roadmap, shared fabric, HDMI mesh, USB transparent, sensor-kit taxonomy, USB 3 matrix); About (About+current-boundary, journal story, accessibility, contributing, legacy, license) -- dropping the pinned 080 nav entry. Landing order: value prop; three CTAs (Start -> Course map -> Safety); 4-6 line 'where things stand' including the required Lesson 080 link; What ADK provides; arc-only course table; build-and-verify; short safety boundary; linkless planned bullets; one-line footer (research/journal/source/roadmap/license). Per-page roles with one canonical source per claim: about.md#current-status owns the full boundary prose; course.md owns per-lesson status (deferring gates to docs/CURRICULUM.md); lessons/index.md is a pure link directory (drop status wall and the stale planned 080 row); components.md becomes a concept page deferring to docs/COMPONENTS.md (ownership), api-supported.md (interfaces), course.md (status); build.md owns make targets (start.md and README link it); delete or stub site/pages/projects/cadence.md in favor of docs/projects/component_project_cadence.md. All check_site.py gates stay satisfiable: the landing keeps its lessons/080 link in the status summary, lessons/index.md keeps its 080 table row, lesson pages are untouched (PDF/sketch links and content markers), and planned rows in README/course.md remain linkless.

findings.issue: The stylesheet targets `body > header`, `body > main`, and `article`, but the mkdocs Bootstrap theme renders `.navbar.bg-primary` and `.container > .col-md-9[role=main]` with none of those elements. The intended 52rem reading measure and header restyle never apply, so body text runs the full ~810px Bootstrap column (~95+ characters per line) in the generic Bootstrap look.
findings.recommendation: Retarget the real markup: `div[role="main"] { max-width: 52rem; }` (keep tables/pre allowed to overflow within it), and delete or repoint the `body > header`/`article` rules. This is the single highest impact-per-risk change: one selector fix restores the designed typography measure site-wide, CSS-only, no checker interaction.

findings.issue: The theme has a real light/dark/auto toggle that flips `data-bs-theme` and swaps highlight.js to github-dark, but site.css hardcodes the light paper palette on `body`, `pre`, `code`, links, and rules with no dark overrides. In dark mode users get a forced-light `pre` background (#fffdf7) with github-dark's light token colors (near-unreadable code), a light body against dark Bootstrap TOC cards and dropdown menus, and low-contrast link green.
findings.recommendation: Restate the palette as Bootstrap variable overrides so the toggle works: set `--bs-body-bg/--bs-body-color/--bs-border-color/--bs-link-color` from the --adk-* tokens under `:root, [data-bs-theme=light]`, and add a `[data-bs-theme=dark]` block with a dark-paper variant (e.g. ink #e8e4d8 on #1d1f1c, panel #26292 4, desaturated accent). Scope `pre, code` backgrounds per theme so hljs github/github-dark each sit on a matching surface. CSS-only, checker-safe.

findings.issue: The landing page's first screen after four buttons is a ~65-line 'Current boundary' blockquote enumerating every lesson's caveats, followed by a 38-row table. The first impression is a wall of legal-style caveat prose with zero imagery, which is the main reason the site reads as unappealing.

Add one pencil illustration beside the intro as a hero image. Wire in the already-styled but unused `.landing-paths` three-column section (site.css lines 123-150) for Course / Library / Safety entry points. Medium risk (link/nav churn) but the largest aesthetic payoff.

findings.issue: The warm paper/ink/forest-green ADK palette never reaches the chrome: the navbar stays Bootstrap's default dark-navy `bg-primary`, the TOC card uses `bg-body-tertiary` gray, and focus/hover states use Bootstrap blue. The page reads as two unrelated designs stacked (generic Bootstrap frame, custom paper content).

findings.issue: No type scale or rhythm is defined: Bootstrap default sizes (h1 2.5rem down to h3) with default system stack, uniform margins, and nothing distinguishing headings from the generic Bootstrap look. Long lesson pages (080 is ~300 lines with 7 h2 sections) have no visual waypoints.

result.summary: The ADK site is mkdocs 1.6.1's default Bootstrap 5 theme with a thin custom stylesheet (site/assets/site.css), and the core diagnosis is that the intended 'paper/ink/pencil' design mostly never reaches the rendered page. (1) About a third of site.css is dead: it styles `body > header`, `body > main`, and `article`, but the theme emits `.navbar.bg-primary` and `.col-md-9[role=main]`, so the 52rem reading measure and header treatment never apply and text runs ~95+ characters per line inside a stock navy Bootstrap frame. (2) Dark mode is genuinely broken: the theme's toggle flips `data-bs-theme` and swaps highlight.js to github-dark, but site.css hardcodes light paper on body/pre/code with no dark overrides, yielding light code surfaces with light token colors and a light body against dark Bootstrap cards. (3) The landing page's first screen is a ~65-line caveat blockquote followed by a 38-row table with zero imagery; the designed `.landing-paths` grid in CSS is used by no page. (4) The signature pencil illustrations — including four fresh, well-compressed 080 diagrams already staged to downloads/assets/ — are absent from lesson 080, the landing page, course map, and lesson index. (5) No type scale, section rhythm, or table treatment exists; the three highest-traffic pages are 38-81-row tables with 'Host verified; bench open' repeated ~70 times, and `table{display:block}` degrades table layout/semantics. Highest impact for least risk, in order: fix the dead selectors so the reading measure applies (one-line CSS); restate the palette as Bootstrap CSS-variable overrides with a `[data-bs-theme=dark]` block; recolor the navbar/TOC to the accent palette; embed the existing 080 pencil PNGs with alt text (checker-safe since check_site.py only requires alt text and resolvable paths); add heading rhythm and compact sticky-header table styling. The larger structural wins — compressing the landing boundary blockquote to a summary plus a dedicated status page, wiring in the landing-paths grid, and splitting course.md into per-arc sections — carry moderate link/nav churn but remain compatible with strict mode as long as nav entries and anchors are added consistently. All CSS-level changes are invisible to `make site-check` (scripts/check_site.py validates links, fragments, alt text, PDFs, and path leaks only).
